pub fn contains_system_principal(value: &Value) -> bool {
    match value {
        Value::Id(id) => id == crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL,
        Value::Array(items) => items.iter().any(contains_system_principal),
        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values().any(contains_system_principal),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Missing optional columns read as null; missing required columns with a
/// literal default read that value. Contextual defaults belong to inserts.
pub fn materialize_optional_fields(row: &mut Value, table: &Table) {
    let fields = match row {
        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields,
        _ => return,
    };
    for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
        if !fields.contains_key(name) {
            if table.maintained.contains_key(name) {
                fields.insert(name.clone(), Value::Int(0));
            } else if kind.is_optional() {
                fields.insert(name.clone(), Value::Null);
            } else if let Some(ColumnDefault::Literal(value)) = table.defaults.get(name) {
                fields.insert(name.clone(), value.clone());
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Borrow complete images; materialize old images only when needed.
pub fn row_image<'a>(row: &'a Value, table: &Table) -> std::borrow::Cow<'a, Value> {
    if table.columns.keys().all(|column| row.field(column).is_ok()) { return std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(row); }
    let mut image = row.clone();
    materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, table);
    std::borrow::Cow::Owned(image)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
/// The type an argument declares as a column type, for value validation.
pub fn arg_as_column(kind: &ArgType) -> Option<ColumnType> {
    Some(match kind {
        ArgType::Cursor | ArgType::Scalar => return None,
        ArgType::Id => ColumnType::Id,
        ArgType::Principal => ColumnType::Principal,
        ArgType::Ref { table } => ColumnType::Ref { table: table.clone() },
        ArgType::Text { max, .. } => ColumnType::Text { max: *max },
        ArgType::Bytes { max } => ColumnType::Bytes { max: *max },
        ArgType::Image { max } => ColumnType::Image { max: *max, once: false },
        ArgType::Video { max } => ColumnType::Video { max: *max },
        ArgType::File { max, types } => ColumnType::File { max: *max, types: types.clone() },
        ArgType::Int => ColumnType::Int,
        ArgType::IntRange { min, max } => ColumnType::IntRange { min: *min, max: *max },
        ArgType::Bool => ColumnType::Bool,
        ArgType::Time => ColumnType::Time,
        ArgType::Json { max_bytes } => ColumnType::Json { max_bytes: *max_bytes },
        ArgType::Optional(inner) => ColumnType::Optional(Box::new(arg_as_column(inner)?)),
        ArgType::List { of, max } => ColumnType::List { of: Box::new(of.as_deref().map(arg_as_column).flatten().unwrap_or(ColumnType::Json { max_bytes: 4096 })), max: *max },
        ArgType::ListRange { of, min, max } => ColumnType::ListRange { of: Box::new(of.as_deref().and_then(arg_as_column).unwrap_or(ColumnType::Json { max_bytes: 4096 })), min: *min, max: *max },
        ArgType::Enum { variants } => ColumnType::Enum { variants: variants.clone() },
        ArgType::Decimal { scale } => ColumnType::Decimal { scale: *scale },
        ArgType::Money { currency, scale } => ColumnType::Money { currency: currency.clone(), scale: *scale },
    })
}

import Quarry.Eval

/-!
# Writes: rule checks and refusals

From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the
writes card:

* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on
  `id` or a declared unique key with a hidden row is `E_RULE`; with a visible
  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
  or the key's `else CODE`.
* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that
  `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` references name also needs read
  authority (`NOT_FOUND`); then its delete closes over `cascade` references,
  refuses `E_REFERENCED` while a `restrict` reference names a closure row
  from outside the closure, clears `set null` references outside it, and
  removes the closure (LLP 3000.039 §3).

The order in which checks run when several fail is not documented; the
model's order is OPEN W1–W6.
-/

namespace Quarry

def notFound : Stop := .refuse "NOT_FOUND"
def eRule : Stop := .refuse "E_RULE"
def eInput : Stop := .refuse "E_INPUT"

def toScalarE : Value → Except Stop Scalar
  | .s x => pure x
  | _ => throw eInput

def scalarsE (fs : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop (List (String × Scalar)) :=
  fs.mapM fun p => do return (p.1, ← toScalarE p.2)

/-- A column value fits its declaration: only a nullable column takes null. -/
def fits (c : ColDecl) (x : Scalar) : Bool := c.nullable || x != .null

/-- The new image of an insert. An absent nullable column is null; an absent
required column refuses with `missing`. Unknown fields refuse `E_INPUT`. -/
def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))
    (missing : Stop) : Except Stop Row := do
  if fields.any fun p => p.1 != "id" && !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
  let cols ← td.cols.mapM fun c => match fields.lookup c.name with
    | some x => if fits c x then pure (c.name, x) else throw eInput
    | none => if c.nullable then pure (c.name, Scalar.null) else throw missing
  return { id := rid, cols }

/-- The next image of an update: the patch replaces named columns. -/
def patchImage (td : TableDecl) (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop Row := do
  if patch.any fun p => !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
  let cols ← old.cols.mapM fun p => match patch.lookup p.1 with
    | some x =>
      match td.cols.find? (·.name == p.1) with
      | some c => if fits c x then pure (p.1, x) else throw eInput
      | none => throw eInput
    | none => pure p
  return { old with cols }

def keyOf (cols : List String) (r : Row) : List (String × Scalar) := cols.map fun c => (c, r.get c)

/-- The first unique key (in order) on which another row (not `except`)
collides with `img`. Keys with a null component never collide (a nullable
unique key permits tied nulls; indexes card). -/
def findClash (rows : List Row) (keys : List (List String)) (img : Row) (except : Option (List Nat)) :
    Option (Nat × Row) :=
  let rec go (i : Nat) : List (List String) → Option (Nat × Row)
    | [] => none
    | k :: ks =>
      let kv := keyOf k img
      if kv.any (·.2 == .null) then go (i + 1) ks
      else match rows.find? (fun r => keyMatch kv r && except != some r.id) with
        | some r => some (i, r)
        | none => go (i + 1) ks
  go 0 keys

/-- The refusal for a visible clash on unique key `i` of `["id"] ++ uniques`
(`withId`) or of `uniques`. -/
def clashCode (td : TableDecl) (withId : Bool) (i : Nat) : Stop :=
  let j := if withId then i - 1 else i
  if withId && i = 0 then .refuse "E_CONSTRAINT"
  else match td.uniqueCodes[j]? with
    | some (some code) => .refuse code
    | _ => .refuse "E_UNIQUE"

def findRow (rows : List Row) (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
  if ks.any (·.2 == .null) then none else rows.find? (keyMatch ks)

-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#7 — expired rows release every logical lookup key.
/-- A write target lookup selects among live rows, rather than selecting a
physical predecessor and rejecting it after it has hidden a live match. -/
def findLiveRow (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (rows : List Row)
    (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
  findRow (rows.filter (unexpired td now)) ks

/-- The result of a write: the row if the viewer can read it afterwards,
else null (`why E_CONFLICT`: results are read-rule gets; OPEN W4 for insert). -/
def resultOf (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
  if readable sch s v t r then r.toValue else .null

def resultOfAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
    (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
  if readableAt sch s v now t r then r.toValue else .null

/-- `guardE b e` continues when `b` holds and refuses `e` otherwise. -/
def guardE (b : Bool) (e : Stop) : Except Stop Unit := if b then .ok () else .error e

def doInsertImage (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
    (img : Row) (clashHidden : Stop) :
    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
  -- Insert authority has already been checked. Remaining unique checks and
  -- the physical insertion use the post-retirement store.
  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
  | some (i, r) => do
    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) clashHidden
    throw (clashCode td true i)
  | none =>
    let s' := s.insertRow t img
    pure (resultOfAt sch s' v now t img, s')

/-- An update's `if` condition: `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable target,
`E_CONFLICT` when false. -/
def condCheck (rd : Bool) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) (old : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
  match cond with
  | some f => do
    guardE rd notFound
    let b ← f old
    guardE b (.refuse "E_CONFLICT")
  | none => pure ()

/-- A secondary unique clash of an update's next image with another row. -/
def clashCheck (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
    (rd : Bool) (old nw : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) td.uniques nw (some old.id) with
  | some (i, r) =>
    throw (if !rd then notFound else if !(readableAt sch s v now t r) then eRule else clashCode td false i)
  | none => pure ()

def doUpdateRow (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
    (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) :
    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
  let nw ← patchImage td old patch
  guardE (td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw })
    (if readableAt sch s v now t old then eRule else notFound)
  condCheck (readableAt sch s v now t old) cond old
  clashCheck sch s v now t td (readableAt sch s v now t old) old nw
  pure (resultOfAt sch (s.replaceRow t old nw) v now t nw, s.replaceRow t old nw)

/-- The id of an absent upsert's new row: from the key, else the patch. -/
def upsertId (ks ps : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop (List Nat) :=
  match ks.lookup "id" with
  | some (.id x) => pure x
  | _ => match ps.lookup "id" with
    | some (.id x) => pure x
    | _ => throw eInput

def insertId (fs : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop (List Nat) :=
  match fs.lookup "id" with
  | some (.id x) => pure x
  | _ => throw eInput

/-! ## Referential actions (LLP 3000.039 §3) -/

/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:
`(child table, column, action)`. -/
def referencing (sch : Schema) (t : String) : List (String × String × OnDelete) :=
  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => td.cols.filterMap fun c =>
    match c.ref, c.onDelete with
    | some p, some a => if p == t then some (td.name, c.name, a) else none
    | _, _ => none

/-- Row `k` names the row with id `i` through column `c`. -/
def names (k : Row) (c : String) (i : List Nat) : Bool := k.get c == .id i

def inClosure (cl : List (String × Row)) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  cl.any fun p => p.1 == t && p.2.id == r.id

/-- The rows one step of cascades reaches from `(t, r)`. -/
def cascadeKids (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : List (String × Row) :=
  (referencing sch t).flatMap fun (c, col, a) =>
    if a == .cascade then ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id).map fun k => (c, k) else []

/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`
bounds the walk (the store's row count suffices). -/
def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)
  | 0, _, acc => acc
  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc
  | f + 1, (t, r) :: rest, acc =>
    let new := (cascadeKids sch s t r).foldl (fun n p => if inClosure (acc ++ n) p.1 p.2 then n else n ++ [p]) []
    closure sch s f (rest ++ new) (acc ++ new)

/-- Some `restrict` reference names a closure row from outside the closure. -/
def restricted (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (cl : List (String × Row)) : Bool :=
  cl.any fun (t, r) => (referencing sch t).any fun (c, col, a) =>
    a == .restrict && (s c).any fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k

def clearCol (r : Row) (c : String) : Row :=
  { r with cols := r.cols.map fun p => if p.1 == c then (p.1, Scalar.null) else p }

/-- Clear every `set null` reference that names a closure row from outside it. -/
def setNulls (sch : Schema) (cl : List (String × Row)) (s : Store) : Store :=
  cl.foldl (fun s (t, r) => (referencing sch t).foldl (fun s (c, col, a) =>
    if a == .setNull then
      ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k).foldl
        (fun s k => s.replaceRow c k (clearCol k col)) s
    else s) s) s

def storeSize (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat := sch.tables.foldl (fun n td => n + (s td.name).length) 0

/-- The store after deleting `old` from `t` with its referential actions, or
`E_REFERENCED`. With no action-carrying reference into `t`, exactly
`removeRow` (LLP 3000.039 §1). -/
def refDelete (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
  let cl := closure sch s (storeSize sch s + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
  if restricted sch s cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
  else pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) (setNulls sch cl s))

/-- Apply actions to the physical store using only the rows that are logically
live as action witnesses. The root may itself be absent from `witnesses`. -/
def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
  let cl := closure sch witnesses (storeSize sch witnesses + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
  else
    let physical := cl.foldl (fun s (parent, row) => (referencing sch parent).foldl (fun s (child, col, action) =>
      if action == .setNull then
        ((witnesses child).filter fun k => names k col row.id && !inClosure cl child k).foldl
          (fun s witness => match (s child).find? fun current => current.id == witness.id with
            | some current =>
              if names current col row.id then s.replaceRow child current (clearCol current col) else s
            | none => s) s
      else s) s) physical
    pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) physical)

/-! ## Expiry retirement (LLP 3000.036.003 §6; LLP 3000.039 §3) -/

def expired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  match td.expire with
  | none => false
  | some c => match r.get c with
    | .int closes => closes <= now
    | _ => false

def stored (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  (s t).any fun current => current.id == r.id

/-- Retire a due row that physically holds an inserted id. The native engine
does this before checking the new image's remaining unique keys, in the same
transaction as the insert. -/
def retireExpiredSameId (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (t : String)
    (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) : Except Stop Store :=
  match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
  | some old =>
    if expired td now old then refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old
    else pure s
  | none => pure s

/-- Whether `insert if absent` has a live unique-key occupant. Native checks
all live unique collisions before retiring an expired same-id predecessor, so
a no-op leaves the physical store and its action children unchanged. -/
def insertIfAbsentClash (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
    (t : String) (td : TableDecl) (img : Row) : Except Stop Bool :=
  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
  | some (_, r) => do
    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) eRule
    pure true
  | none => pure false

/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)

def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)

def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
  | some (_, rs) => rs
  | none => fallback t

-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
root can be retired immediately. -/
def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
  let rows := sch.tables.foldl (fun rows td =>
    let physical := rows.store s
    (physical td.name).foldl (fun rows r =>
      let physical := rows.store s
      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
        | .error _ => rows
      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
  rows.store s

-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — same-id replacement authorizes, retires with actions, then inserts.
/-- Apply one write to the store. -/
def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
  | .insert t fields ifAbsent =>
    match cx.schema.table? t with
    | none => throw eInput
    | some td => do
      let fs ← scalarsE fields
      let rid ← insertId fs
      let img ← buildImage td rid fs eInput
      -- Native refusal order authorizes the proposed image while the expired
      -- predecessor is still present, then retires it and applies its actions.
      guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) eRule
      if ifAbsent then
        let clashes ← insertIfAbsentClash cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img
        if clashes then pure (.null, s)
        else
          let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
          doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
      else
        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
  | .update t key patch cond =>
    match cx.schema.table? t with
    | none => throw eInput
    | some td => do
      let ks ← scalarsE key
      let ps ← scalarsE patch
      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
      | none => throw notFound
      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
  | .upsert t key patch =>
    match cx.schema.table? t with
    | none => throw eInput
    | some td => do
      let ks ← scalarsE key
      let ps ← scalarsE patch
      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps none
      | none => do
        let rid ← upsertId ks ps
        let img ← buildImage td rid (ks ++ ps) notFound
        guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) notFound
        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img notFound
  | .delete t key =>
    match cx.schema.table? t with
    | none => throw eInput
    | some td => do
      let ks ← scalarsE key
      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
      | none => throw notFound
      | some old => do
        guardE (td.delete.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some old })
          (if readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old then eRule else notFound)
        guardE ((referencing cx.schema t).isEmpty || readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old) notFound
        pure (.null, ← refDeleteFrom cx.schema (unexpiredStore cx.schema s cx.now) s t old)

end Quarry

//! One wire fence for engine semantics an older decoder must not ignore.
//! Constraint is strictly parsed by 0.2.33, unlike Schema's optional fields.
use super::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

// Private remote derive: the schema has one wire field list, and callers
// cannot accidentally invoke an unchecked inherent Schema::deserialize.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(remote = "Schema")]
struct Wire {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    receipts: Vec<ReceiptFamily>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    receipt_dependencies: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    source_reservations: BTreeMap<String, reservations::WriteReservation>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    legacy_receipt_prediction: bool,
    #[serde(skip)]
    legacy_semantic_capabilities: LegacySemanticCapabilities,
    tables: BTreeMap<String, Table>,
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    #[serde(skip)]
    authored_indexes: inspection::AuthoredIndexes,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    delivery: Vec<DeliveryBinding>,
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    #[serde(skip)]
    delivery_lookup: crate::engine::delivery::Lookup,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    timelines: Vec<timeline::Timeline>,
    #[serde(default)]
    maintains: Vec<Maintain>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Auth::is_default")]
    auth: Auth,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    effects: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    schedules: Vec<Schedule>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    operations: BTreeMap<String, Execution>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    unique_refusals: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, UniqueRefusal>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    action_specs: BTreeMap<String, ActionSpec>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    effect_specs: BTreeMap<String, WorkSpec>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    routes: BTreeMap<String, RouteSpec>,
}

// Add a capability and its schema predicate here in one line. This is both
// the derivation and the decoder's allowlist; authors never declare it.
const CAPABILITIES: &[(&str, fn(&Schema) -> bool)] = &[
    ("source-write-reservations-v2", |s| s.source_reservations.values().any(|p| p.birth.is_some())),
    ("source-write-reservations-v1", |s| !s.source_reservations.is_empty()),
    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — older devices must not execute newly eligible
    // writes using their receipt-derived maintenance path.
    ("receipt-derived-prediction-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| s.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target))
        || s.has_receipt_columns()),
    ("rule-reference-v2", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t|
        [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.any_term(&|term| matches!(term, RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. })))
        || t.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { key, .. } if key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some()))))),
    ("rule-reference", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.has_reference()))),
    ("declarative-receipts-v4", |s| !s.receipts.is_empty()),
    ("owner-key-coverage", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.own_keys.is_some())),
    ("ephemeral", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.ephemeral.is_some())),
    ("field-authority", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.written_by.is_empty() || t.update_transition)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — an older decoder refuses ordered insert rules rather than misjudging them.
    ("insert-rule-order", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered(&t.rules.insert))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — a decoder that orders only int/time in insert rules refuses a money or decimal order by name.
    ("insert-rule-order-units", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered_units(t, &t.rules.insert))),
    ("row-keyed-view", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.row_key.is_some())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — older devices compute canonical-JSON
    // aggregate ids and would silently miss digest-addressed target rows.
    ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.is_none())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#8 — an older engine or device must not delete with the old (orphaning) semantics.
    ("reference-actions", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.on_delete.is_empty())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — pre-Wave-12 devices neither retire expiry
    // through actions nor queue an unproved same-id physical predecessor.
    ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", |s| s.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.is_expiring() && s.is_referenced(name))),
    ("read-through", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.through.is_some()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.parent_key.is_some() || !m.aliases.is_empty())),
    // Device projections keep column metadata but omit private maintains.
    ("maintained-column", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.maintained.is_empty()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.private.is_some())),
    ("recorded-attribution", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.recorded.is_empty())),
    ("sequence-by", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.sequences.is_empty())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — an older decoder names the bounded int it cannot check.
    ("int-range", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.values().any(int_range))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — civil keys and calendar schedules.
    ("calendar-month", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.indexes.values().any(|i| i.components.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Calendar(key) if key.civil()))))
        || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.computed.values().any(|key| key.civil()))),
    ("calendar-schedule", |s| s.schedules.iter().any(|schedule| schedule.months > 0)),
    ("timeline", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 1)),
    ("timeline-v2", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 2)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#3 — an older device would page a merged plan as an eager merge and refuse its server cursors; it refuses the backend by name.
    ("branch-merge-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_merge)),
    ("branch-membership-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#15 — v2 fences metered uncapped discovery and row-id point lanes from v1 devices.
    ("branch-pages-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v2)),
    ("branch-pages-v3", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v3)),
    ("branch-pages-v4", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v4)),
    ("branch-membership-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership_v2)),
    // Source slots alter negative coverage, prediction and application row projection.
    ("timeline-event-slots", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.keys().any(|field| timeline::is_slot(field)))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.3 — a decoder that ignored `also` would hold only the first arm and lose rows.
    ("union-audience", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(Sync::is_union))),
    ("time-audiences-v1", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some())),
];

fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
    match kind {
        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

impl Schema {
    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
    }
    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
    }
}

impl Serialize for Schema {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        let required = self.required_capabilities();
        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
        let mut wire = self.clone();
        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
        }
        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut carriers = 0;
        let mut legacy = false;
        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
            let mut recorded = 0;
            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
                    carriers += 1;
                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
                    false
                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
                    recorded += 1;
                    false
                } else { true }
            });
            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
            }
            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
        }
        for name in &declared {
            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
            }
        }
        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
            else { required.remove(cap); }
        }
        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
        }
        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
        }
        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
        }
        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
        }
        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
        Ok(schema)
    }
}

import Quarry.Write

/-!
# Running a program

`run` takes (schema, helpers, store, viewer, program, arguments, ceiling)
to an outcome. This is the function the later harness oracle calls.
-/

namespace Quarry

/-- An outcome. A query answers with data, `complete` and the returned
page's continuation (`next`, null when none), or is unavailable (a cut
scalar read), or refuses. A mutation commits a result and a new store, or
refuses (and changes nothing). -/
inductive Outcome where
  | answer (data : Value) (complete : Bool) (next : Value)
  | unavailable
  | committed (result : Value) (store : Store)
  | refused (code : String)

/-- The world of a query: the view; every write refuses. -/
def queryHooks : Hooks View where
  view _ vw := vw
  apply _ _ _ := throw (.refuse "E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT")

/-- The world of a mutation: the store; reads see its visible rows. -/
def storeHooks : Hooks Store where
  view cx s := visibleRowsAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now
  apply := applyWrite

-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
sweep. -/
abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)

structure MutationWorld where
  store : Store
  changed : ChangedRows := []

/-- The explicit address of an insert-like write that reached its write arm.
This retains a structurally identical expired replacement for commit-end
retirement, while excluding `insert if absent` live-clash no-ops. -/
def RWrite.changedExplicitId? (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
  | .insert t fields ifAbsent => do
    let td ← cx.schema.table? t
    let fs ← (scalarsE fields).toOption
    let rid ← (insertId fs).toOption
    let img ← (buildImage td rid fs eInput).toOption
    if ifAbsent && (findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now))
        (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none).isSome
    then none
    else some (t, rid)
  | .upsert t key patch =>
    match key.lookup "id" with
    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
      | _ => none
  | _ => none

def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)

def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
    | .error e => .error e
    | .ok (value, store) =>
      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
      let changed := match rw.changedExplicitId? cx w.store with
        | some address => changed ++ [address]
        | none => changed
      .ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })

/-- Retire only rows written by this mutation whose final image is already
expired. A restrict refusal aborts the mutation; cascade and set-null actions
are in the same transition. -/
def retireExpiredChanged (sch : Schema) (now : Int) : Store → ChangedRows → Except Stop Store
  | s, [] => pure s
  | s, (t, rid) :: rest =>
    match sch.table? t with
    | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    | some td =>
      match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
      | some row =>
        if expired td now row then do
          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest

def bindArgs (params : List Param) (args : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop Env :=
  params.mapM fun p => match args.lookup p.name with
    | some v => pure (p.name, (v, none))
    | none => if p.optional then pure (p.name, (.null, none)) else throw (.refuse "E_INPUT")

def defaultFuel : Nat := 100000

structure Case where
  schema : Schema
  helpers : List Helper := []
  store : Store
  viewer : List Nat
  now : Int := 0
  program : Program
  args : List (String × Value) := []
  budget : Option Nat := none
  /-- Run only the server expiry sweep and return its resulting store. -/
  sweepOnly : Bool := false

def Case.ctx (c : Case) : Ctx :=
  { schema := c.schema, viewer := c.viewer, now := c.now, helpers := c.helpers, budget := c.budget,
    mutation := c.program.kind == .mutation }

def flowValue : Flow → Value × Value
  | .normal => (.null, .null)
  | .ret v nx => (v, nx.getD .null)

def runQuery (c : Case) : Outcome :=
  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
  | .ok env =>
    let vw := visibleRowsAt c.schema c.store c.viewer c.now
    match (execStmts queryHooks defaultFuel c.ctx vw env c.program.body).run {} with
    | .ok ((fl, _, _), rs) => let (v, nx) := flowValue fl; .answer v rs.complete nx
    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
    | .error .unavailable => .unavailable

def runMutation (c : Case) : Outcome :=
  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
  | .ok env =>
    match (execStmts mutationHooks defaultFuel c.ctx { store := c.store } env c.program.body).run {} with
    | .ok ((fl, w, _), _) => match retireExpiredChanged c.schema c.now w.store w.changed with
      | .ok s' => .committed (flowValue fl).1 s'
      | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
      | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
    | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"

def run (c : Case) : Outcome :=
  if c.sweepOnly then .committed .null (sweepExpired c.schema c.store c.now)
  else match c.program.kind with
    | .query => runQuery c
    | .mutation => runMutation c

end Quarry

import Quarry.Store

/-!
# Maintained aggregate identity

The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
identity while publishing the new version.
-/

namespace Quarry

/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
migration. -/
def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"

/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
to this logical model. -/
def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble

theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
  simp [maintainedIdV1]

/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
  omega

def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }

structure MaintainedState where
  version : Nat
  rows : List Row

/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }

theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl

theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]

theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]

example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
  maintainedIdV1_length _

end Quarry

import Quarry.Syntax

/-!
# Rows, stores, rules and visibility

A store maps each table name to its rows. Rules are evaluated against the
whole store: an `exists t[..]` probe is an exact-key existence test that does
not consult `t`'s own read rule (OPEN R1). A row is *visible* to a viewer
when its table's read rule holds for it; every read the evaluator performs
goes through `visibleRows`, so the read semantics in `Eval.lean` never sees
a hidden row (`Disclosure.lean`).
-/

namespace Quarry

structure Row where
  id : List Nat
  cols : List (String × Scalar)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

def Row.get (r : Row) (c : String) : Scalar :=
  if c = "id" then .id r.id else (r.cols.lookup c).getD .null

def Row.toValue (r : Row) : Value :=
  .row (("id", .s (.id r.id)) :: r.cols.map fun p => (p.1, .s p.2))

/-- The store: the rows of each table. -/
abbrev Store := String → List Row

def Store.empty : Store := fun _ => []

def Store.set (s : Store) (t : String) (rs : List Row) : Store :=
  fun t' => if t' = t then rs else s t'

def Store.insertRow (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Store := s.set t (s t ++ [r])
def Store.replaceRow (s : Store) (t : String) (old nw : Row) : Store :=
  s.set t ((s t).map fun r => if r.id = old.id then nw else r)
def Store.removeRow (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Store :=
  s.set t ((s t).filter fun r => r.id ≠ old.id)

/-- The images a rule may name. -/
structure Imgs where
  self : Option Row := none
  old : Option Row := none
  next : Option Row := none

def Imgs.get (im : Imgs) : Img → Option Row
  | .self => im.self
  | .old => im.old
  | .next => im.next

def Term.eval (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) : Term → Option Scalar
  | .col i c => (im.get i).map (·.get c)
  | .viewer => some (.id v)
  | .param _ => none
  | .lit x => some x

/-- Evaluate every component of a key probe. -/
def probeTerms (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) (key : List (String × Term)) :
    Option (List (String × Scalar)) :=
  key.mapM fun p => Option.map (fun x => (p.1, x)) (p.2.eval v im)

/-- Null returns no row only when it occurs in the selected unique point key.
Nullable equalities outside that key are residual predicates and may match
null. An empty `point` keeps the older all-components convention for the
hand-written core model. -/
def probeKey (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) (point : List String)
    (key : List (String × Term)) :
    Option (List (String × Scalar)) :=
  match probeTerms v im key with
  | none => none
  | some ks =>
    let selected := if point.isEmpty then ks else ks.filter fun p => point.contains p.1
    if selected.length == (if point.isEmpty then ks.length else point.eraseDups.length)
        && !(selected.any fun p => p.2 == .null)
    then some ks else none

def keyMatch (ks : List (String × Scalar)) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  ks.all fun p => decide (r.get p.1 = p.2)

/-- Rule evaluation against the whole store `s`, for viewer `v`. -/
def Rule.eval (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) : Rule → Bool
  | .allow => true
  | .deny => false
  | .eq a b => match a.eval v im, b.eval v im with
    | some x, some y => decide (x = y)
    | _, _ => false
  | .ne a b => match a.eval v im, b.eval v im with
    | some x, some y => decide (x ≠ y)
    | _, _ => false
  | .probe t point key => match probeKey v im point key with
    | some ks => (s t).any (keyMatch ks)
    | none => false
  | .and a b => a.eval s v im && b.eval s v im
  | .or a b => a.eval s v im || b.eval s v im
  | .not a => !(a.eval s v im)

/-- The tables a rule probes. -/
def Rule.probes : Rule → List String
  | .probe t _ _ => [t]
  | .and a b | .or a b => a.probes ++ b.probes
  | .not a => a.probes
  | _ => []

/-- The row columns (of the `self` image) a rule reads. -/
def Term.selfCols : Term → List String
  | .col .self c => [c]
  | _ => []

/-- Every term a rule compares or probes with, left to right. -/
def Rule.terms : Rule → List Term
  | .eq a b | .ne a b => [a, b]
  | .probe _ _ key => key.map (·.2)
  | .and a b | .or a b => a.terms ++ b.terms
  | .not a => a.terms
  | .allow | .deny => []

def Rule.selfCols (r : Rule) : List String := r.terms.flatMap Term.selfCols

/-- The rule with each term replaced by `f` of it. -/
def Rule.mapTerms (f : Term → Term) : Rule → Rule
  | .eq a b => .eq (f a) (f b)
  | .ne a b => .ne (f a) (f b)
  | .probe t point key => .probe t point (key.map fun p => (p.1, f p.2))
  | .and a b => .and (a.mapTerms f) (b.mapTerms f)
  | .or a b => .or (a.mapTerms f) (b.mapTerms f)
  | .not a => .not (a.mapTerms f)
  | .allow => .allow
  | .deny => .deny

/-- The disjuncts of a rule's top-level `or` (a rule that is not an `or` is
its own single disjunct). -/
def Rule.disjuncts : Rule → List Rule
  | .or a b => a.disjuncts ++ b.disjuncts
  | .allow => [.allow]
  | .deny => [.deny]
  | .eq a b => [.eq a b]
  | .ne a b => [.ne a b]
  | .probe t point key => [.probe t point key]
  | .and a b => [.and a b]
  | .not a => [.not a]

/-- A rule without `not`. Over fewer rows a positive rule can only lose
probe witnesses, so one true over the caller's view is true over the store
(`Rule.eval_mono`); the engine likewise never takes a negated probe as a
grant (LLP 3000.036 §12.1). -/
def Rule.positive : Rule → Bool
  | .not _ => false
  | .and a b | .or a b => a.positive && b.positive
  | .allow | .deny | .eq .. | .ne .. | .probe .. => true

/-- Fold only rule truth values that remain known after pin substitution.
Boolean literal comparisons match the engine's required-boolean pin proof;
in particular, a nullable `null` pin is not treated as boolean `false`.
Probes are never folded, so normalization cannot turn a negated probe into a
page grant (LLP 3000.036 §14). -/
-- @ref LLP 3000.036.001#9 — the formal classifier and executable model share prefix-normalized guards.
def Rule.normalize : Rule → Rule
  | .eq (.lit (.bool a)) (.lit (.bool b)) => if a == b then .allow else .deny
  | .eq (.lit a) (.lit b) => if a == b then .allow else .eq (.lit a) (.lit b)
  | .eq .viewer .viewer => .allow
  | .eq a b => .eq a b
  | .ne (.lit (.bool a)) (.lit (.bool b)) => if a != b then .allow else .deny
  | .ne (.lit a) (.lit b) => if a != b then .ne (.lit a) (.lit b) else .deny
  | .ne .viewer .viewer => .deny
  | .ne a b => .ne a b
  | .and a b =>
      match a.normalize, b.normalize with
      | .allow, b' => b'
      | a', .allow => a'
      | .deny, _ | _, .deny => .deny
      | a', b' => .and a' b'
  | .or a b =>
      match a.normalize, b.normalize with
      | .allow, _ | _, .allow => .allow
      | .deny, b' => b'
      | a', .deny => a'
      | a', b' => .or a' b'
  | .not a => match a.normalize with
      | .allow => .deny
      | .deny => .allow
      | a' => .not a'
  | .allow => .allow
  | .deny => .deny
  | .probe t point key => .probe t point key

/-- A term with each pinned row column replaced by its pinned value. -/
def Term.pin (ps : List (String × Scalar)) : Term → Term
  | .col .self c => match ps.lookup c with
    | some x => .lit x
    | none => .col .self c
  | t => t

/-- A rule with each pinned row column replaced by its pinned value: the
verdict the rule gives every row the pins select (`Rule.eval_pin`). -/
def Rule.pin (ps : List (String × Scalar)) (r : Rule) : Rule := r.mapTerms (Term.pin ps)

def readable (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  match sch.table? t with
  | some td => td.read.eval s v { self := some r }
  | none => false

/-- The rows of `t` the viewer may read. Every read goes through this. -/
def visibleRows (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) : List Row :=
  (s t).filter (readable sch s v t)

/-- Whether a row has reached its table's lower read lifetime. Null is open;
the checked schema guarantees that a non-null lifetime value is a time. -/
-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — lower read lifetimes filter every logical read at the server clock.
def opened (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  match td.notBefore with
  | none => true
  | some c => match r.get c with
    | .null => true
    | .int opens => opens <= now
    | _ => false

/-- Whether a row remains before its table's upper read lifetime. Null has no
upper bound; the checked schema guarantees that a non-null value is a time. -/
-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — upper read lifetimes filter every logical read before physical cleanup.
def unexpired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  match td.expire with
  | none => true
  | some c => match r.get c with
    | .null => true
    | .int closes => now < closes
    | _ => false

def live (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool := opened td now r && unexpired td now r

/-- Referential actions ignore expired child images but still govern a child
whose lower read lifetime has not opened yet, matching the physical engine. -/
def unexpiredStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
  match sch.table? t with
  | some td => (s t).filter (unexpired td now)
  | none => []

/-- The physical store with rows outside their logical lifetime removed. Rule
probes use this store too, so a future or expired row cannot authorize work. -/
def openedStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
  match sch.table? t with
  | some td => (s t).filter (live td now)
  | none => []

/-- Read-rule visibility for one image at a request clock. The image may be a
physical write target, while every probe it performs sees only opened rows. -/
def readableAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
    (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
  match sch.table? t with
  | some td => live td now r && td.read.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r }
  | none => false

/-- Request-time visibility, including the server-enforced lower read lifetime. -/
def visibleRowsAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
    (t : String) : List Row :=
  (s t).filter (readableAt sch s v now t)

/-- What a read can observe: the visible rows of each table. -/
abbrev View := String → List Row

end Quarry

import Quarry.Run

/-!
# Write authority

**No write succeeds unless the corresponding rule holds.** A successful write
either leaves the store unchanged (`insert … if absent` on a visible clash)
or is one authorized `Step`: an insert whose insert rule admits the new
image, an update whose update rule admits (old, next) for a row that exists,
or a delete whose delete rule admits the row. Rules are evaluated in the
opened projection of the store as it stood immediately before that write
(`applyWrite_authorized`).

A whole mutation's store transition is a chain of such steps
(`mutation_authorized`).
-/

namespace Quarry

inductive Step (sch : Schema) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) : Store → Store → Prop
  | insert {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {r : Row} :
      sch.table? t = some td → td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r } = true →
      Step sch v now s (s.insertRow t r)
  | update {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old nw : Row} :
      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
      td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw } = true →
      Step sch v now s (s.replaceRow t old nw)
  /-- A delete whose delete rule admits the row, with the referential
  actions the schema declares on the rows naming it (LLP 3000.039 §4.1: the
  parent's delete authorizes a declared cascade or set null). -/
  | delete {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
      td.delete.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some old } = true →
      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
      Step sch v now s s'
  /-- An expired same-id row is retired inside an insert transaction before
  the replacement image's remaining constraints are checked. -/
  | retire {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
      Step sch v now s s'
  /-- A same-id replacement is one authorized transition: its insert rule is
  checked against the pre-retirement store, then the expired predecessor's
  actions run, then the new image is inserted. -/
  | replaceExpired {s retired : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old img : Row} :
      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
      td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some img } = true →
      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok retired →
      Step sch v now s (retired.insertRow t img)

inductive Steps (sch : Schema) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) : Store → Store → Prop
  | refl (s : Store) : Steps sch v now s s
  | step {s s' s'' : Store} : Step sch v now s s' → Steps sch v now s' s'' → Steps sch v now s s''

theorem Steps.trans {sch v now} {a b d : Store} (h1 : Steps sch v now a b) (h2 : Steps sch v now b d) :
    Steps sch v now a d := by
  induction h1 with
  | refl => exact h2
  | step h _ ih => exact .step h (ih h2)

theorem Steps.of_step_or_eq {sch v now} {a b : Store} (h : b = a ∨ Step sch v now a b) : Steps sch v now a b := by
  rcases h with h | h
  · subst h; exact .refl _
  · exact .step h (.refl _)

theorem bind_ok {ε α β : Type} {x : Except ε α} {f : α → Except ε β} {b : β}
    (h : (x >>= f) = .ok b) : ∃ a, x = .ok a ∧ f a = .ok b := by
  cases x with
  | error e => cases h
  | ok a => exact ⟨a, rfl, h⟩

theorem guardE_ok {b : Bool} {e : Stop} {u : Unit} (h : guardE b e = .ok u) : b = true := by
  unfold guardE at h; split at h <;> simp_all

theorem findRow_mem {rows : List Row} {ks} {r : Row} (h : findRow rows ks = some r) : r ∈ rows := by
  unfold findRow at h
  split at h
  · cases h
  · exact List.mem_of_find?_eq_some h

theorem findLiveRow_mem {td : TableDecl} {now : Int} {rows : List Row} {ks} {r : Row}
    (h : findLiveRow td now rows ks = some r) : r ∈ rows := by
  exact (List.mem_filter.1 (findRow_mem (by simpa [findLiveRow] using h))).1

theorem doInsertImage_ok {sch : Schema} {s : Store} {v : List Nat} {now : Int}
    {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {img : Row} {clashHidden : Stop}
    {val : Value} {s' : Store}
    (h : doInsertImage sch s v now t td img clashHidden = .ok (val, s')) :
    s' = s.insertRow t img := by
  unfold doInsertImage at h
  split at h
  · obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
    cases h
  · cases h; rfl

theorem doUpdateRow_ok {sch s v now t td old patch cond val s'}
    (h : doUpdateRow sch s v now t td old patch cond = .ok (val, s')) :
    ∃ nw, td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw } = true ∧
      s' = s.replaceRow t old nw := by
  unfold doUpdateRow at h
  obtain ⟨nw, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
  obtain ⟨_, hg, h⟩ := bind_ok h
  obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
  obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
  cases h
  exact ⟨nw, guardE_ok hg, rfl⟩

theorem retireExpiredSameId_result {sch : Schema} {s s' : Store} {now : Int}
    {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {rid : List Nat}
    (h : retireExpiredSameId sch s now t td rid = .ok s') :
    s' = s ∨ ∃ old, old ∈ s t ∧ expired td now old = true ∧
      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' := by
  unfold retireExpiredSameId at h
  split at h
  · rename_i old hold
    split at h
    · rename_i hexp
      exact .inr ⟨old, findRow_mem hold, hexp, h⟩
    · cases h
      exact .inl rfl
  · cases h
    exact .inl rfl

theorem retireExpiredSameId_steps {sch s s' v now t td rid}
    (ht : sch.table? t = some td)
    (h : retireExpiredSameId sch s now t td rid = .ok s') :
    Steps sch v now s s' := by
  rcases retireExpiredSameId_result h with h | ⟨old, hold, hexp, href⟩
  · subst h; exact .refl _
  · exact .step (.retire ht hold hexp href) (.refl _)

theorem retireThenInsert_authorized {sch : Schema} {s s0 s' : Store} {v : List Nat}
    {now : Int} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {rid : List Nat} {img : Row}
    {clashHidden : Stop} {val : Value}
    (ht : sch.table? t = some td)
    (ha : td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some img } = true)
    (hr : retireExpiredSameId sch s now t td rid = .ok s0)
    (hi : doInsertImage sch s0 v now t td img clashHidden = .ok (val, s')) :
    Steps sch v now s s' := by
  have hi := doInsertImage_ok hi
  subst hi
  rcases retireExpiredSameId_result hr with hs | ⟨old, hold, hexp, href⟩
  · subst hs
    exact .step (.insert ht ha) (.refl _)
  · exact .step (.replaceExpired ht hold hexp ha href) (.refl _)

/-- **Referential actions change nothing a schema does not declare**
(LLP 3000.039 §1): a delete from a table no action-carrying reference names
removes exactly that row, as every delete did before. -/
theorem refDelete_without_actions {sch : Schema} {s : Store} {t : String} {old : Row}
    (h : referencing sch t = []) : refDelete sch s t old = .ok (s.removeRow t old) := by
  have hk : cascadeKids sch s t old = [] := by simp [cascadeKids, h]
  have hc : ∀ f, closure sch s (f + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)] = [(t, old)] := by
    intro f; cases f <;> simp [closure, hk]
  simp only [refDelete, hc, restricted, setNulls, List.any_cons, List.any_nil, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil]
  simp [h, pure, Except.pure]

/-- **Write authority, one write.** -/
theorem applyWrite_authorized {cx : Ctx} {s s' : Store} {rw : RWrite} {val : Value}
    (h : applyWrite cx s rw = .ok (val, s')) : Steps cx.schema cx.viewer cx.now s s' := by
  cases rw with
  | insert t fields ifAbsent =>
    simp only [applyWrite] at h
    split at h
    · cases h
    · rename_i td htd
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      obtain ⟨img, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      obtain ⟨_, hg, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      cases ifAbsent with
      | false =>
        simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false] at h
        obtain ⟨s0, hr, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        exact retireThenInsert_authorized htd (guardE_ok hg) hr h
      | true =>
        simp only [ite_true] at h
        obtain ⟨clashes, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        cases clashes with
        | false =>
          simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false] at h
          obtain ⟨s0, hr, h⟩ := bind_ok h
          exact retireThenInsert_authorized htd (guardE_ok hg) hr h
        | true =>
          simp only [ite_true] at h
          cases h
          exact .refl _
  | update t key patch cond =>
    simp only [applyWrite] at h
    split at h
    · cases h
    · rename_i td htd
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      split at h
      · cases h
      · rename_i old hold
        obtain ⟨nw, hr, h⟩ := doUpdateRow_ok h
        subst h; exact .step (.update htd (findLiveRow_mem hold) hr) (.refl _)
  | upsert t key patch =>
    simp only [applyWrite] at h
    split at h
    · cases h
    · rename_i td htd
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      split at h
      · rename_i old hold
        obtain ⟨nw, hr, h⟩ := doUpdateRow_ok h
        subst h
        exact .step (.update htd (findLiveRow_mem hold) hr) (.refl _)
      · obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        obtain ⟨img, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        obtain ⟨_, hg, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        obtain ⟨s0, hrs, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        exact retireThenInsert_authorized htd (guardE_ok hg) hrs h
  | delete t key =>
    simp only [applyWrite] at h
    split at h
    · cases h
    · rename_i td htd
      obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
      split at h
      · cases h
      · rename_i old hold
        obtain ⟨_, hg, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        obtain ⟨_, -, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        obtain ⟨s2, hd, h⟩ := bind_ok h
        cases h
        exact .step (.delete htd (findLiveRow_mem hold) (guardE_ok hg) hd) (.refl _)

end Quarry

namespace Quarry

theorem sbind_ok {α β : Type} {x : EM α} {f : α → EM β} {rs : RS} {r : β × RS}
    (h : (x >>= f).run rs = .ok r) : ∃ a rs1, x.run rs = .ok (a, rs1) ∧ (f a).run rs1 = .ok r := by
  simp only [StateT.run_bind] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨a, rs1⟩, h1, h2⟩ := bind_ok h
  exact ⟨a, rs1, h1, h2⟩

theorem liftE_ok {α : Type} {x : Except Stop α} {rs : RS} {a : α} {rs' : RS}
    (h : (liftE x).run rs = .ok (a, rs')) : x = .ok a := by
  unfold liftE at h
  cases x with
  | error e => cases h
  | ok b => simp [StateT.run, Except.map] at h; rw [h.1]

/-- Statement execution changes the world only through `Hooks.apply`: any
relation on worlds that is reflexive, transitive and contains every applied
write contains the whole execution. -/
theorem execStmts_inv {W : Type} (H : Hooks W) (cx : Ctx) (R : W → W → Prop) (hrefl : ∀ w, R w w)
    (htrans : ∀ a b d, R a b → R b d → R a d)
    (happ : ∀ w rw val w', H.apply cx w rw = .ok (val, w') → R w w') :
    ∀ fuel w env ss rs fl w' env' rs',
      (execStmts H fuel cx w env ss).run rs = .ok ((fl, w', env'), rs') → R w w' := by
  intro fuel
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
    intro w env ss rs fl w' env' rs' h
    simp [execStmts, refuse, StateT.run, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift] at h
    cases h
  | succ fuel ih =>
    intro w env ss rs fl w' env' rs' h
    cases ss with
    | nil =>
      simp only [execStmts, StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
      cases h; exact hrefl w
    | cons s ss =>
      cases s with
      | assign x e =>
        simp only [execStmts] at h
        obtain ⟨p, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        exact ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h
      | require c code =>
        simp only [execStmts] at h
        obtain ⟨⟨v, _⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        obtain ⟨b, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        split at h
        · exact ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h
        · simp [refuse, StateT.run, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift] at h; cases h
      | ret e =>
        simp only [execStmts] at h
        obtain ⟨⟨v, nx⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        simp only [StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
        cases h; exact hrefl w
      | ite c th el =>
        simp only [execStmts] at h
        obtain ⟨⟨v, _⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        obtain ⟨b, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        obtain ⟨⟨fl1, w1, env1⟩, rs3, h1, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        have r1 := ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h1
        split at h
        · simp only [StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
          cases h; exact r1
        · exact htrans _ _ _ r1 (ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h)
      | write bind op =>
        simp only [execStmts] at h
        obtain ⟨rs0, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        obtain ⟨rw, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        obtain ⟨⟨val, w1⟩, rs3, h1, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
        exact htrans _ _ _ (happ _ _ _ _ (liftE_ok h1)) (ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h)

theorem mutationHooks_apply_authorized {cx : Ctx} {w w' : MutationWorld}
    {rw : RWrite} {val : Value}
    (h : mutationHooks.apply cx w rw = .ok (val, w')) :
    Steps cx.schema cx.viewer cx.now w.store w'.store := by
  change (match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
    | Except.error e => Except.error e
    | Except.ok (value, store) =>
      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
      let changed := match rw.changedExplicitId? cx w.store with
        | some address => changed ++ [address]
        | none => changed
      Except.ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })) = Except.ok (val, w') at h
  split at h
  · cases h
  · rename_i result store happ
    cases h
    exact applyWrite_authorized happ

/-- Commit-end expiry retirement is a chain of referential-action retirement
steps. Rows absent from the final store and rows whose final image is live are
identity transitions. -/
theorem retireExpiredChanged_steps {sch : Schema} {v : List Nat} {now : Int}
    (changed : ChangedRows) : ∀ s s',
    retireExpiredChanged sch now s changed = .ok s' → Steps sch v now s s' := by
  induction changed with
  | nil =>
    intro s s' h
    simp only [retireExpiredChanged, pure, Except.pure] at h
    cases h
    exact .refl _
  | cons address rest ih =>
    rcases address with ⟨t, rid⟩
    intro s s' h
    simp only [retireExpiredChanged] at h
    split at h
    · exact ih _ _ h
    · rename_i td htd
      split at h
      · exact ih _ _ h
      · rename_i row hrow
        split at h
        · rename_i hexp
          obtain ⟨s1, href, hrest⟩ := bind_ok h
          exact .step (.retire htd (findRow_mem hrow) hexp href) (ih _ _ hrest)
        · exact ih _ _ h

/-- **Write authority, whole mutation.** Every committed mutation's store is
reached from the original by a chain of authorized writes followed by the
transactional retirement of final images that were born or updated expired. -/
theorem mutation_authorized {c : Case} {res : Value} {s' : Store}
    (hk : c.program.kind = .mutation) (hs : c.sweepOnly = false)
    (h : run c = .committed res s') :
    Steps c.schema c.viewer c.now c.store s' := by
  simp [run, hs, hk, runMutation] at h
  split at h
  · cases h
  · cases h
  · split at h
    · rename_i fl w env1 rs1 hx
      split at h
      · rename_i hret
        cases h
        have hbody : Steps c.schema c.viewer c.now c.store w.store :=
          execStmts_inv mutationHooks c.ctx
            (fun a b => Steps c.schema c.viewer c.now a.store b.store)
            (fun _ => Steps.refl _) (fun _ _ _ => Steps.trans)
            (fun _ _ _ _ happ => mutationHooks_apply_authorized happ)
            _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ hx
        exact hbody.trans (retireExpiredChanged_steps w.changed w.store s' hret)
      · cases h
      · cases h
    · cases h
    · cases h

end Quarry
