//! The generation barrier checks predecessor audiences before destructive projection.
// @ref LLP 3000.014#7-activation — pinned time, child scan, capture before validation, atomic publication.
use crate::{
    error::RuntimeError,
    rows::{Bounds, Dir, Rows},
    schema::{RuleExpr, Schema, Table, through::PARENT_DEADLINE},
    value::Value,
};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";

/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
    mut tables: Vec<String>,
    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let after = cursors
        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
        tables.rotate_left(next);
    }
    tables
}

pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {
    cursors.insert(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR.into(), vec![Value::String(table.into())]);
}

/// Only inherited batches need staging. Preserve the streaming path for
/// existing schemas, including large fixture imports.
pub(crate) fn ancestor_order<'a, I>(
    schema: &Schema,
    rows: I,
) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + 'a>
where
    I: IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    I::IntoIter: 'a,
{
    if schema.tables.values().all(|t| t.through.is_none()) {
        return Box::new(rows.into_iter());
    }
    let order = schema.through_order();
    let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    rows.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| order.iter().position(|n| n == name).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
    Box::new(rows.into_iter())
}

fn refusal(name: &str, count: usize, reason: &str, samples: &[String]) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::Structural {
        code: "E_READ_THROUGH_ADOPT",
        message: format!(
            "{name}: {count} child rows cannot adopt read through: {reason}; sample ids/parent values [{}]; rewrite: reconcile the named audience fields and live parents in a bridge release, then `snapback4 deploy <dir> --restore-dormant` (guide rules)",
            samples.join(", ")
        ),
    }
}

fn sample(samples: &mut Vec<String>, row: &Value, reference: &str, parent: &str) {
    fn bounded(text: &str) -> &str {
        let mut end = text.len().min(256);
        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
            end -= 1;
        }
        &text[..end]
    }
    if samples.len() < 5 {
        let id = row
            .field("id")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
        let value = row
            .field(reference)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
        samples.push(format!(
            "{}: {reference} -> {parent}[{}]",
            bounded(id),
            bounded(value)
        ));
    }
}

fn rows(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    name: &str,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
    loop {
        let page = tx.scan(name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
        if page.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        for (row, key) in page {
            bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
            visit(row)?;
        }
    }
}

fn correspondence(
    child: &RuleExpr,
    parent: &RuleExpr,
) -> Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>> {
    if child.is_uniformly_readable() && parent.is_uniformly_readable() {
        return Some(Default::default());
    }
    fn walk(
        a: &serde_json::Value,
        b: &serde_json::Value,
        map: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
    ) -> bool {
        use serde_json::Value::*;
        match (a, b) {
            (Object(a), Object(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
                if let (Some(String(a)), Some(String(b))) = (a.get("Field"), b.get("Field")) {
                    if map.get(a).is_some_and(|old| old != b)
                        || map.iter().any(|(old, v)| v == b && old != a)
                    {
                        return false;
                    }
                    map.insert(a.clone(), b.clone());
                    true
                } else {
                    a.iter()
                        .all(|(k, a)| b.get(k).is_some_and(|b| walk(a, b, map)))
                }
            }
            (Array(a), Array(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
                a.iter().zip(b).all(|(a, b)| walk(a, b, map))
            }
            _ => a == b,
        }
    }
    let mut map = Default::default();
    walk(
        &serde_json::to_value(child).ok()?,
        &serde_json::to_value(parent).ok()?,
        &mut map,
    )
    .then_some(map)
}

/// The retirement phase shared by activation and its read-only occupancy
/// preview. Selection and the predecessor deadline predicate live here once;
/// checking a candidate must not count a row this phase would remove.
pub(crate) struct Retirement<'a> {
    affected: Vec<(String, &'a Table)>,
    now: i64,
}

impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {
        let affected = next
            .through_order()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|name| {
                let next = &next.tables[&name];
                let old = previous.table(&name)?;
                Self::changes_lifetime(next,old).then_some((name, old))
            })
            .collect();
        Self { affected, now }
    }

    fn changes_lifetime(next:&Table,old:&Table) -> bool {
        next.through != old.through || next.through.is_some() && (next.expire != old.expire || next.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires_image(next:&Table,old:&Table,row:&Value,now:i64) -> bool {
        (next.through!=old.through || next.expire!=old.expire || old.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field))) && old.expired(row,now)
    }

    pub(crate) fn affects(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.affected.iter().any(|(table, _)| table == name)
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires(&self, name: &str, row: &Value) -> bool {
        self.affected
            .iter()
            .find(|(table, _)| table == name)
            .is_some_and(|(_, old)| old.expired(row, self.now))
    }
}

/// Capture barrier for an authoritative adapter's uncommitted generation.
pub fn activate(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
    activate_retained(tx, next, previous, now, &Default::default())
}

pub(crate) fn activate_retained(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    now: i64,
    retained: &std::collections::BTreeSet<String>,
) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut shortened = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    let Some(previous) = previous else {
        return Ok(shortened);
    };
    // Previous indexes and row images still exist. Every affected expired row
    // retires under its old deadline, before a new default or capture can revive it.
    let retirement = Retirement::new(next, previous, now);
    for (name, old) in retirement.affected.iter().rev() {
        rows(tx, name, |row| {
            if retirement.retires(name, &row) {
                tx.delete(name, old, &row)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
    }
    // Compare all predecessor images before any ancestor is recaptured.
    for (name, _) in &retirement.affected {
        let Some(t) = &next.tables[name].through else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(old) = previous.table(name).filter(|t| t.through.is_none()) else {
            continue;
        };
        let parent = previous
            .table(&t.parent)
            .ok_or_else(|| refusal(name, 0, "the previous parent schema is absent", &[]))?;
        let map = correspondence(&old.rules.read, &parent.rules.read);
        let mut invalid = 0;
        let mut samples = Vec::new();
        rows(tx, name, |row| {
            // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#10-wave-10-release-lifecycle-amendment — historical capture restoration needs no audience recapture.
            if retained.contains(name) && row.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).is_ok() && t.fields.keys().all(|f|row.field(f).is_ok()) {return Ok(());}
            let Some(map) = &map else {
                invalid += 1;
                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
                return Ok(());
            };
            let row = crate::schema::row_image(&row, old);
            let parent_row = row
                .field(&t.reference)
                .ok()
                .and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
                .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
                .transpose()?
                .flatten();
            let matches = parent_row.as_ref().is_some_and(|image| {
                !parent.expired(image, now) && {
                    let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, parent);
                    map.iter()
                        .all(|(child, p)| row.field(child).ok() == image.field(p).ok())
                }
            });
            if !matches {
                invalid += 1;
                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if invalid > 0 {
            return Err(refusal(
                name,
                invalid,
                "missing, ambiguous or disagreeing predecessor audience correspondence",
                &samples,
            ));
        }
    }
    for name in next.through_order() {
        let table = &next.tables[&name];
        let Some(t) = &table.through else {
            continue;
        };
        let parent = &next.tables[&t.parent];
        let recapture = previous.table(&name).and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref()) != Some(t);
        let mut invalid = 0;
        let mut samples = Vec::new();
        rows(tx, &name, |old| {
            let mut row = old.clone();
            // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#2-retain-by-default — restored audience/deadline captures retain their original lifetime.
            let historical = retained.contains(&name) && old.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).is_ok();
            if recapture && (!historical || t.fields.keys().any(|field| old.field(field).is_err()))
            {
                let parent_row = old
                    .field(&t.reference)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
                    .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
                    .transpose()?
                    .flatten();
                // @ref LLP 3000.014#7-activation — previous-schema expiry was retired before projection; a newly due deadline must propagate, not veto adoption.
                let Some(parent_row) = parent_row else {
                    invalid += 1;
                    sample(&mut samples, &old, &t.reference, &t.parent);
                    return Ok(());
                };
                if historical {
                    let mut fresh = row.clone();
                    super::through::stamp(parent, t, &parent_row, &mut fresh)?;
                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
                        for field in t.fields.keys().filter(|field| old.field(field).is_err()) {
                            fields.insert(field.clone(), fresh.field(field)?.clone());
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    super::through::stamp(parent, t, &parent_row, &mut row)?;
                }
            }
            table.recompute_deadline(&mut row)?;
            let before = previous.table(&name).and_then(|table| table.deadline(&old));
            if table
                .deadline(&row)
                .is_some_and(|after| before.is_none_or(|before| after < before))
            {
                *shortened.entry(name.clone()).or_default() += 1;
            }
            tx.put(&name, table, &row, Some(&old))?;
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if invalid > 0 {
            return Err(refusal(&name, invalid, "missing parent", &samples));
        }
    }
    Ok(shortened)
}

/// Trusted restoration validates the existing immutable captures; it never stamps them.
pub fn validate_restore(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, now: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for name in schema.through_order() {
        let table = &schema.tables[&name];
        let Some(t) = &table.through else {
            continue;
        };
        let parent = &schema.tables[&t.parent];
        let mut invalid = 0;
        let mut samples = Vec::new();
        rows(tx, &name, |row| {
            let found = row
                .field(&t.reference)
                .ok()
                .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
                .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
                .transpose()?
                .flatten();
            let matches = found.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| {
                (!parent.expired(p, now) || table.expired(&row, now)) && {
                    let p = crate::schema::row_image(p, parent);
                    t.fields
                        .iter()
                        .all(|(field, source)| row.field(field).ok() == p.field(source).ok())
                        && row.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).ok()
                            == Some(&parent.deadline(&p).map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null))
                }
            });
            if !matches {
                invalid += 1;
                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if invalid > 0 {
            return Err(refusal(
                &name,
                invalid,
                "restored captures do not match a live parent",
                &samples,
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn validate_indexes(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
        let mut checks: Vec<_> = table
            .indexes
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, i)| i.unique)
            .map(|(name, i)| (name, i.components.len(), 1, true))
            .collect();
        for constraint in &table.constraints {
            if let crate::schema::Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
                let (index, _) = table
                    .indexes
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().starts_with(by))
                    .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} cap has no index")))?;
                checks.push((index, by.len(), u64::from(*max), false));
            }
        }
        for (index, width, max, nulls_distinct) in checks {
            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
            let mut previous = None;
            let mut count = 0;
            loop {
                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
                if page.is_empty() {
                    break;
                }
                for (_, key) in page {
                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
                    bounds.after = Some(full);
                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
                        count += 1;
                    } else {
                        previous = Some(group);
                        count = 1;
                    }
                    if count > max {
                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
                        )));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
    pub fn seed_server_rows(
        &mut self,
        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
            ));
        }
        let order = self.schema.through_order();
        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
        let count = rows.len() as u64;
        for (name, row) in rows {
            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
            self.upsert(
                &name,
                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
            )?;
        }
        self.check_final_exists()?;
        Ok(count)
    }

    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
            ));
        }
        let now = self
            .context
            .now
            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
        let mut count = 0;
        let mut visited = 0;
        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
        for name in tables {
            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
                continue;
            };
            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
            let mut bounds = due.clone();
            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
            while visited < limit {
                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
                    runner
                        .tx
                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
                })?;
                if page.is_empty() {
                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
                        bounds = due.clone();
                        wrapped = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                }
                let page_len = page.len();
                for (row, key) in page {
                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
                    visited += 1;
                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
                        Ok(false) => {},
                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
                    }
                }
                if page_len < batch {
                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
                        bounds = due.clone();
                        wrapped = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(count)
    }
}

## Summary

Snapback 4 is one of two parallel candidates for the successor to Snapback 2,
and the sibling of Snapback 3, not its successor. It builds
[LLP 2000.000](./2000.000-keep-the-core-flip-two-substrates.rfc.md) as
written: the Snapback 2 core kept verbatim, two substrates flipped up front —
resources metered at runtime instead of priced statically, and a client that
replicates the viewer's declared partition instead of caching receipted
results — proved first on the hub fixture, with a deterministic simulator as
the primary harness. Snapback 3 ([LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md), led by
Codex / GPT-6 Astra) keeps the same two questions open and discovers their
answers in its first slice. Snapback 2 ([LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md))
continues as the incumbent and the control. All three are judged by one
pre-registered comparison on one clock.

This document records the author's decisions of 2026-09-12 that created the
track, restates the bet on one page so a reader can orient without the brief,
fixes the bakeoff protocol, draws the fence, and plans the first four weeks.
The design argument and its evidence stay in LLP 2000.000. Only running code
will bind (`rules/RULES.md`).

## 1. Decisions (author, 2026-09-12)

On 2026-09-12 Charlie Cheever asked whether Claude Fable 5.1 should lead a
Snapback 4 while Codex / GPT-6 Astra leads Snapback 3 and Snapback 2
continues, "and see which one turns out best." The lead answered yes with
conditions; the author accepted them ("Sounds good") and asked for this
document. The decisions below are therefore the lead's proposal as accepted
by the author. Where the author has not separately ruled, the text says so.

1. **Three tracks, one comparison.** Snapback 2 continues as the incumbent
   and the control. Snapback 3 builds LLP 2000; Snapback 4 builds LLP
   2000.000. This is a bakeoff of *bets* — discover the substrates in the
   slice versus decide them first — not of models. The result will say more
   about the bets than about the leads, and §3 is written so that it can.
2. **The name is Snapback 4.** Siblings, not a sequence: "4" does not mean
   "after 3." A separate number gives the track its own corpus root,
   directory, package identity and data directory with no rename when the
   bakeoff resolves, and files never move in LLP. If Snapback 4 loses, it is
   a number that never shipped. "Snapback 3b" was considered and rejected:
   it reads as a variant of 3, and this is a different bet.
3. **Snapback 4 builds LLP 2000.000 as written.** Its §14 open questions are
   the lead's to decide inside the track, recorded in §7 as they are
   decided. The author rules on the bar, the comparison and promotion (§3).
4. **One owner on the core.** The lead writes the engine, the store and the
   client contract. Codex lanes build the fixture generator, the reference
   applications, the device witnesses and the periphery. Blind reviews from
   two model families are reserved for the two disclosure-sensitive
   mechanisms: partition inversion of read rules (LLP 2000.000 §7.1) and
   the meter's cut behaviour on non-uniform scans (LLP 2000.000 §6). This
   departs from the standing rule that Codex codes and Claude orchestrates,
   deliberately, for the core only.
5. **The clock is four weeks** from the first commit under `snapback4/` to
   the first slice running on the hub fixture. At the clock the author kills
   the track, merges its substrates into a survivor, or continues it. There
   is no third month without a ruling.
6. **Shared and not shared.** Shared with Snapback 3: the LLP corpus, the
   Clique harness and scorers, the fixtures, the briefs, and the simulator
   once either track has one. Not shared: code, except the Snapback 2 pieces
   both are expected to copy (LLP 2000.000 §5.1).
7. **Snapback 2 keeps shipping and freezes new substrate work for the
   duration.** Fix-forward, the loop bar, acquisition and papercuts continue;
   no new certificate axes, client custody mechanisms or ceiling changes.
   This is accepted here as a condition of the bakeoff. Making it binding on
   concurrent Snapback 2 sessions needs one line in `rules/NOT-DOING.md`'s
   Moves ledger, which this document does not write.
8. **Reading load.** This root, updated in place, and one append-only
   journal, `snapback4/JOURNAL.md`. Sub-LLPs only for a decision that must
   outlive the journal. No panels beyond decision 4's two reviews.

## 2. The bet on one page

**Keep verbatim from Snapback 2** (LLP 2000.000 §5.1): the rule language
with its uniformity and hoist analysis, `decided_true` and the
structural-fact refusals; one data language, Quarry, with `--` comments,
`require … else CODE`, `shape`, `merge`, `walk`, `chunk`; the value model
and its conformance corpus; typed read and write states with no silent state
and the refusal envelope `{code, family, site, message, rewrite, guide}`; the
successor classifier (widening additive, checked narrowing, exact projection
ownership); `deliver`'s engine-computed audience, tombstones and
`bootstrap`; `schedule`, `job`, `chunk` and rehearsal; personas; `init`,
`dev`, `check`, `doctor`, `run`, `test`, `why`, `trace`, `guide`; H0
`deploy`, `rollback`, `secret`; channels; assets; the word-prefix index.

**Flip 1 — certify authorization, meter resources** (LLP 2000.000 §6). The
certificate keeps every read site's shape, uniformity, completeness class
and prediction eligibility, and stops pricing bytes and steps. A
deterministic meter charges examined rows, index entries, rule probes,
steps, heap, output and rows written as the program runs, on the server and

    74	    /// Reopen the persisted compiled generation; subsequent transactions refuse
    75	    /// if another connection activates a successor.
    76	    pub fn open(mut client: Client, name: &str) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    77	        let name = namespace(name)?;
    78	        client.batch_execute(&format!("SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
    79	        let row = client.query_one("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
    80	        if row.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
    81	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
    82	        }
    83	        let schema = decode(row.get(1))?;
    84	        let programs = decode(row.get(2))?;
    85	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    86	        // Existing immutable stores adopt this portable admission policy at open.
    87	        // Return one offending index and its exact count, never its row payloads.
    88	        if let Some(row) = client.query(
    89	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
    90	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
    91	        )?.first() {
    92	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
    93	        }
    94	        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, None)
    95	    }

    97	    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — read-session storage and all other upgrades
    98	    // commit together, only after every open/adoption check has succeeded.
    99	    fn attach(client: Client, mut schema: Schema, programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>, create: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   100	        let mut store = Store::new(client);
   101	        let tx = store.opening_transaction()?;
   102	        tx.batch("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s'; SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   103	        if let Some(name) = create {
   104	            tx.batch(&format!("CREATE SCHEMA {name}; SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
   105	            tx.batch(store::DDL)?;
   106	            tx.execute("INSERT INTO _backend VALUES (true,$1,$2,$3)",
   107	                &[&store::VERSION, &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs)])?;
   108	        }
   109	        tx.query("SELECT seq FROM _head WHERE singleton FOR UPDATE", &[])?;
   110	        // Admission must use the backend that survived the wait for the head.
   111	        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.
   112	        let held = tx.query("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?.remove(0);
   113	        if held.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
   115	        }
   116	        let held_schema: Schema = decode(held.get(1))?;
   117	        let held_programs: BTreeMap<String, Program> = decode(held.get(2))?;
   118	        supported(&held_schema, &held_programs)?;
   119	        if held_schema.hash() != schema.hash() || canonical_json(&held_programs) != canonical_json(&programs) {
   120	            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend changed while opening; reopen its current generation".into()));
   121	        }
   122	        // Even a no-op ALTER takes an exclusive table lock. Reopening an
   123	        // upgraded store must remain possible while another reader holds it.
   124	        for (column, ddl) in [
   125	            ("generation", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
   126	            ("through_shortened", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN through_shortened TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"),
   127	            ("maintained_identity_version", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN maintained_identity_version TEXT"),
   128	        ] {
   129	            let exists: bool = tx.query("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = '_backend'::regclass AND attname = $1 AND NOT attisdropped)", &[&column])?[0].get(0);
   130	            if !exists { tx.batch(ddl)?; }
   131	        }
   132	        // Repeat admission under the head fence used by physical adoption.
   133	        if let Some(row) = tx.query(
   134	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
   135	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
   136	        )?.first() {
   137	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
   138	        }
   139	        tx.batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sequences (parent TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, value BIGINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(parent, id));")?;
   140	        tx.batch(store::READ_SESSIONS_DDL)?;
   141	        tx.batch("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq_kind;")?;
   142	        caps::install(&tx, &schema)?;
   143	        let generation = contribution_upgrade::install(&tx, &mut schema)?;
   144	        let generation = maintained_identity_upgrade::install(&tx, &schema, create.is_some(), generation)?;
   145	        // Retain the adapter's ordinary connection limits on successful open.
   146	        tx.batch("SET statement_timeout = '5s'; SET lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   147	        tx.commit()?;
   148	        store.generation = generation;
   149	        schema.prepare_delivery_lookup();
   150	        Ok(Self { store, schema, programs, ceilings: Ceilings::default(), mode: WriteMode::Serialized, retries: 0, precharge: Metered::default(), expiry_after: BTreeMap::new() })
   151	    }

   182	
   183	    pub fn query_with_delivery(&mut self, name: &str, mut context: Context, manifest: super::DeliveryManifest) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
   184	        context.generation = self.generation();
   185	        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))?;
   186	        if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query {
   187	            return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(format!("{name} is not a query")).into());
   188	        }
   189	        super::server_query_allowed(&self.schema, name)?;
   190	        validate::validate_inputs(&self.schema, program, &mut context.args)?;
   191	        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
   192	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   193	        let seq = tx.next_seq()? - 1;
   194	        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, context, Meter::new(self.ceilings, Cut::Cap), seq);
   195	        runner.meter.used = self.precharge;
   196	        let data = runner.run(program)?;
   197	        runner.charge_output(&data)?;
   198	        let (delivery, delivery_meter) = match manifest { super::DeliveryManifest::Build => runner.delivery_manifest(&data), super::DeliveryManifest::Skip => (None, None) };
   199	        let outcome = QueryOutcome { decoration_expiry: runner.decoration_expiry, search_rows: runner.search_rows.take(), search_scopes: None, delivery, delivery_meter, ephemeral: None,
   200	            unavailable: runner.query_unavailable,
   201	            complete: runner.meter.capped_at.is_none()
   202	                && runner.word_cut_at.is_none()
   203	                && !runner.non_uniform
   204	                && !runner.page_overflow
   205	                && !runner.value_source_incomplete
   206	                && !runner.page_position_lost(),
   207	            cut: runner.read_cut(),
   208	            capped_at: runner.meter.capped_at.clone(),
   209	            word_cut_at: runner.word_cut_at.clone(),
   210	            next: runner.outcome_next_cursor()?,
   211	            data,
   212	            seq,
   213	            metered: runner.meter.used,
   214	            tables: runner.read_tables.iter().cloned().collect(),
   215	            next_expiry: runner.next_expiry.get(),
   216	        };
   217	        drop(runner);
   218	        tx.rollback()?;
   219	        Ok(outcome)
   220	    }
   221	
   222	    pub fn replay(&mut self, viewer: &str, op: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
   223	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   224	        let receipt = tx.applied(viewer, op)?;
   225	        tx.rollback()?;
   226	        receipt.as_deref().map(MutationOutcome::from_receipt).transpose()
   227	    }
   228	
   229	    /// Compare wire identity before decoding against the installed program.
   230	    // @ref LLP 3000.009#5.1 — an id binds the admitted operation and arguments.
   231	    fn replay_mutation(&mut self, viewer: &str, id: &str, name: &str, args_digest: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
   232	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   233	        let receipt = tx.applied_bound(viewer, id, name, args_digest)?;
   234	        tx.rollback()?;
   235	        receipt.as_deref().map(MutationOutcome::from_receipt).transpose()
   236	    }
   237	
   238	    pub fn mutate(&mut self, name: &str, op: Option<&str>, mut context: Context) -> Result<MutationOutcome, RuntimeError> {
   239	        context.generation = self.generation();
   240	        let wire_args = if op.is_some() { context.wire_args.take().unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::Value::Object(crate::wire::map_to_json(&context.args))) }
   241	            else { serde_json::Value::Null };
   242	        let args_digest = crate::store::payload_digest(&wire_args);
   243	        // Preserve the bound replay-before-validation contract, including
   244	        // unknown or renamed programs. Never return a historical result row.
   245	        if let Some(op) = op
   246	            && let Some(outcome) = self.replay_mutation(&context.viewer, op, name, &args_digest)?
   247	        {
   248	            return Ok(outcome);
   249	        }
   250	        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {
   251	            self.schema.check_delivery(name, context.delivery_fingerprint.as_deref()).err()
   252	                .unwrap_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))
   253	        })?.clone();
   254	        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
   255	        if context.entropy == 0 {
   256	            context.entropy = crate::ids::seed();
   257	        }
   258	        // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — retries rerun Quarry, rules, maintains, and bookkeeping together
   259	        for attempt in 0..=32 {
   260	            match self.mutate_once(&program, op, context.clone(), &args_digest) {
   261	                Err(error) if retry_transaction(&error) && attempt < 32 => {
   262	                    self.retries += 1;
   263	                    let delay = (100_u64 << attempt.min(6)) + crate::ids::seed() % 250;
   264	                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_micros(delay));
   265	                }
   266	                outcome => return outcome,
   267	            }
   268	        }
   269	        unreachable!()
   270	    }

   122	    /// Stable ancestor order; admission rejects cycles before execution.
   123	    pub fn through_order(&self) -> Vec<String> {
   124	        fn depth(schema: &Schema, name: &str, seen: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> usize {
   125	            if !seen.insert(name.into()) {
   126	                return 0;
   127	            }
   128	            schema
   129	                .table(name)
   130	                .and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref())
   131	                .map_or(0, |t| 1 + depth(schema, &t.parent, seen))
   132	        }
   133	        let mut names: Vec<_> = self.tables.keys().cloned().collect();
   134	        names.sort_by_key(|name| (depth(self, name, &mut BTreeSet::new()), name.clone()));
   135	        names
   136	    }
   137	}

     5	//! the model's case JSON, and through `quarry-oracle` (`snapback4/lean`,
     6	//! `lake build`), one long-lived process per worker that answers one tagged
     7	//! outcome per line. A case the emitter cannot translate is `Unsupported`
     8	//! under the emitter's named reason, never a pass.
     9	//!
    10	//! **The engine side.** The engine over SQLite (the ordinary in-memory
    11	//! server store) at `Ceilings::default()`, the ceilings a production server
    12	//! runs, not the case's stored budget; the model runs unbounded (its meter is
    13	//! abstract, OPEN M1).
    14	//!
    15	//! **Compared fields** (README, "How the harness compares"):
    16	//!
    17	//! - `kind`: answer, unavailable, refused, committed;
    18	//! - `code`: the refusal code (sites are not modelled);
    19	//! - `data` / `result`: exact, both sides as tagged values, so an id never
    20	//!   compares equal to a text (OPEN V1); rows compare as field maps;
    21	//! - `complete`: exact;
    22	//! - `next`: presence only (OPEN C1). When both carry one, each side
    23	//!   continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared
    24	//!   (`continuation-*`), until both are exhausted;

    26	//!   (`post-*`): the engine's store, and the model's committed store (or the
    27	//!   original store after a refusal).
    28	//!
    29	//! Meter fields, cut sites, `tables` and `seq` are not compared. Expiry
    30	//! sweeps advance both stores before the following program is compared.
    31	//!
    32	//! **Signatures** are `lean--{field}--{engine}~{model}`, each side's stable
    33	//! class (a refusal code, `unavailable`, `committed`, or the data's shape).

    65	/// Bring this checkout's `quarry-oracle` up to date with its model sources
    66	/// (`lake build quarry-oracle`, under a second when current). A merge or
    67	/// checkout that changes `lean/` leaves the previous executable in `.lake`,
    68	/// and the harness would report that older model's choices as disagreements
    69	/// (2026-10-12: a stale pre-guard oracle on the merged `sb4-loop` tree showed
    70	/// `lean--complete--complete~incomplete`). Nothing is done when
    71	/// `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE` names the oracle (the caller vouches for it; a
    72	/// campaign's workers inherit the refreshed path that way) or when `lake` is
    73	/// not installed (a missing oracle still refuses at `LeanProcess::spawn`).
    74	pub fn refresh() -> Result<(), String> {
    75	    if std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE").is_some() {
    76	        return Ok(());
    77	    }
    78	    let dir = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean");
    79	    // Keep the optional-tool path read-only, including a checkout whose model
    80	    // directory is not writable. A version probe writes no Lake build artifacts.
    81	    match Command::new("lake").arg("--version").current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    82	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    83	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
    84	            return Ok(());
    85	        }
    86	        Err(e) => return Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
    87	        Ok(_) => {} // The build below reports actual toolchain/configuration errors.
    88	    }
    89	    // @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — concurrent refreshes must not write the same Lake artifacts.
    90	    let cache = dir.join(".lake");
    91	    fs::create_dir_all(&cache).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh cache: {e}"))?;
    92	    let refresh_lock = OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true)
    93	        .open(cache.join("snapback4-refresh.lock")).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    94	    refresh_lock.lock().map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    95	    match Command::new("lake").args(["build", "quarry-oracle"]).current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    96	        Ok(output) if output.status.success() => Ok(()),
    97	        Ok(output) => Err(format!(
    98	            "`lake build quarry-oracle` failed in {}: {}{}",
    99	            dir.display(),
   100	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
   101	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
   102	        )),
   103	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
   104	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
   105	            Ok(())
   106	        }
   107	        Err(e) => Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
   108	    }
   109	}

   111	/// One `quarry-oracle` process: a JSON case per line in, an outcome per line out.
   112	pub struct LeanProcess {
   113	    child: Child,
   114	    stdin: ChildStdin,
   115	    stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
   116	}
   117	impl LeanProcess {
   118	    pub fn spawn() -> Result<Self, String> {
   119	        let path = oracle_path();
   120	        if !path.is_file() {
   121	            return Err(format!(
   122	                "Lean oracle missing: {} (run `cd snapback4/lean && lake build`, or set SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE)",
   123	                path.display()
   124	            ));
   125	        }
   126	        let mut child = Command::new(&path)
   127	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
   128	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
   129	            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
   130	            .spawn()
   131	            .map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
   132	        let stdin = child.stdin.take().unwrap();
   133	        let stdout = BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap());
   134	        Ok(Self { child, stdin, stdout })
   135	    }
   136	    pub fn ask(&mut self, case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   137	        writeln!(self.stdin, "{case}").map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle write: {e}"))?;
   138	        self.stdin.flush().map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle flush: {e}"))?;
   139	        let mut line = String::new();
   140	        let n = self.stdout.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle read: {e}"))?;
   141	        if n == 0 {
   142	            return Err("Lean oracle exited".into());
   143	        }
   144	        let answer: Json = serde_json::from_str(&line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle answer {line:?}: {e}"))?;
   145	        if answer["kind"] == "error" {
   146	            // A case the model cannot decode is an emitter defect, never a verdict.
   147	            return Err(format!("Lean oracle refused the case: {}", answer["error"]));
   148	        }
   149	        Ok(answer)
   150	    }
   151	}
   152	impl Drop for LeanProcess {
   153	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   154	        let _ = self.child.kill();
   155	        let _ = self.child.wait();

   160	    static PROCESS: RefCell<Option<LeanProcess>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };

   163	/// Ask this thread's oracle process, starting it on first use and once
   164	/// more if it has died.
   165	pub fn ask(case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   166	    PROCESS.with(|cell| {
   167	        let mut slot = cell.borrow_mut();
   168	        if slot.is_none() {
   169	            *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   170	        }
   171	        match slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case) {
   172	            Err(e) if e == "Lean oracle exited" => {
   173	                *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   174	                slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case)
   175	            }
   176	            other => other,
   177	        }
   178	    })
   179	}

   181	/// The engine's value as the model's tagged value; rows as field maps.
   182	pub fn engine_value(v: &snapback4_core::Value) -> Json {
   183	    use snapback4_core::Value as V;
   184	    match v {
   185	        V::Null => json!({"null": null}),
   186	        V::Bool(b) => json!({"bool": b}),
   187	        V::Int(n) => json!({"int": n.to_string()}),
   188	        V::String(s) => json!({"text": s}),
   189	        V::Id(s) => json!({"id": s}),
   190	        V::Bytes(b) => json!({"bytes": b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect::<String>()}),
   191	        V::Row(fs) | V::Map(fs) => json!({"row": fs.iter().map(|(k, x)| (k.clone(), engine_value(x))).collect::<Map<_, _>>()}),
   192	        V::Array(xs) => json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(engine_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()}),
   193	    }
   194	}
   195	
   196	/// The model's tagged value with rows as field maps (its rows are ordered pairs).
   197	pub fn model_value(v: &Json) -> Json {
   198	    if let Some(xs) = v.get("arr").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   199	        return json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(model_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()});
   200	    }
   201	    if let Some(fs) = v.get("row").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   202	        let mut m = Map::new();
   203	        for p in fs {
   204	            m.insert(p[0].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(), model_value(&p[1]));
   205	        }
   206	        return json!({"row": m});
   207	    }
   208	    v.clone()
   209	}

   212	    v.as_object().and_then(|o| o.keys().next().cloned()).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".into())
   213	}

I found a possible formal/runtime mismatch in commit-end retirement order. Lean processes rows in mutation-change order; runtime sorts them by table and id. I’m checking a cascade/restrict case where that could change whether the mutation commits.

   101	fn legacy_digest_recovery<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S, initial: bool) {
   102	    let current = legacy_digest_store(store);
   103	    let error = match Opening::Kept.open(Borrowed(store)) {
   104	        Err(error) => error,
   105	        Ok(_) => panic!("offline device executed a kept pre-digest backend"),
   106	    };
   107	    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
   108	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   109	    let before = tx.outbox_entries().unwrap();
   110	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   111	    let opening = if initial { Opening::Initial(current) } else { Opening::Install(current) };
   112	    drop(opening.open(Borrowed(store)).expect("a current backend must recover a kept legacy backend"));
   113	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   114	    assert_eq!(tx.outbox_entries().unwrap(), before, "semantic upgrade preserves queued writes");
   115	    assert_eq!(tx.meta("device:generation").unwrap().as_deref(), Some("2"));
   116	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   117	}

   134	// Borrow the real store so a refused opening leaves it available for inspection.
   135	struct Borrowed<'a, S>(&'a mut S);
   136	impl<S: DeviceStore> DeviceStore for Borrowed<'_, S> {
   137	    type Tx<'a> = S::Tx<'a> where Self: 'a;
   138	    fn install(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   139	        self.0.install(schema, metadata, reset)
   140	    }
   141	    fn install_checked(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   142	        self.0.install_checked(schema, metadata, reset, expected)
   143	    }
   144	    fn meta(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> { self.0.meta(key) }
   145	    fn set_meta(&mut self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { self.0.set_meta(key, value) }
   146	    fn transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Self::Tx<'_>, RuntimeError> { self.0.transaction() }
   147	}

   149	fn refused_reopen_preserves<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) {
   150	    let backend = plain();
   151	    drop(Device::open_store(Borrowed(store), Some(backend.clone())).unwrap());
   152	    let row = object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into()))]);
   153	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   154	    tx.put("t", &backend.schema.tables["t"], &row, None).unwrap();
   155	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   156	    let mut future = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();
   157	    future["schema"]["tables"]["t"]["constraints"] = json!([{"Capabilities":["future-derivation"]}]);
   158	    store.set_meta("device:backend", &future.to_string()).unwrap();
   159	    let mut replacement = backend;
   160	    replacement.generation = 2; // Without the fence this resets the held row.
   161	    let before = store.transaction().unwrap().meta_prefix("").unwrap();
   162	    for opening in [Opening::Install(replacement.clone()), Opening::Kept, Opening::Initial(replacement)] {
   163	        let error = match opening.open(Borrowed(store)) {
   164	            Err(error) => error,
   165	            Ok(_) => panic!("unsupported kept backend accepted during reopening"),
   166	        };
   167	        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
   168	        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   169	        assert_eq!(tx.meta_prefix("").unwrap(), before, "refusal must preserve all metadata");
   170	        assert_eq!(tx.get("t", "kept").unwrap(), Some(row.clone()), "refusal must preserve rows");
   171	    }
   172	}

   191	// Linux counterpart of schema-capabilities.test.mjs's published-engine fence.
   192	// Include DDL (indexes/triggers/columns), every table and every stored value.
   193	// The refusal contract covers schema/rows, integrity and freelist count.
   194	// WAL identity is asserted for the small no-spill cases below; a large rolled
   195	// back migration may change free-page contents or retain uncommitted frames
   196	// (LLP 3000.033 §1.3).
   197	fn sqlite_dump(path: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> {
   198	    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open_with_flags(path, rusqlite::OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY).unwrap();
   199	    let mut tables = vec!["sqlite_schema".to_string()];
   200	    tables.extend(db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name").unwrap()
   201	        .query_map([], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0)).unwrap().map(Result::unwrap));
   202	    let mut snapshot = tables.into_iter().map(|name| {
   203	        let mut stmt = db.prepare(&format!("SELECT * FROM \"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""))).unwrap();
   204	        let columns = stmt.column_count();
   205	        let mut rows = stmt.query_map([], |r| (0..columns).map(|i| r.get::<_, rusqlite::types::Value>(i)).collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>())
   206	            .unwrap().map(|r| format!("{:?}", r.unwrap())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   207	        rows.sort();
   208	        (name, rows)
   209	    }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   210	    let integrity: String = db.query_row("PRAGMA integrity_check", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   211	    assert_eq!(integrity, "ok");
   212	    let free: i64 = db.query_row("PRAGMA freelist_count", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   213	    snapshot.push(("PRAGMA integrity_check/freelist_count".into(), vec![integrity, free.to_string()]));
   214	    snapshot
   215	}

   560	fn every_hop(catalog: &Catalog, info: &TableInfo, rule: &RuleDecl, diagnostic: &mut Diagnostic) {
   561	    fn leaves<'a>(value: &'a Expr, out: &mut Vec<&'a Expr>) {
   562	        match value {
   563	            Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" || op == "or" => { leaves(left, out); leaves(right, out); }
   564	            other => out.push(other),
   565	        }
   566	    }

   568	    leaves(&rule.value, &mut parts);

   595	        if error.code == "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR" && rule.effect == Effect::Update && rule.bindings.is_empty()
   596	            && error.rewrite == "write this as a named transition" {
   597	            let source = super::rule_operator::named_update_source(&rule.value);
   598	            error.rewrite = format!("name both row images: `{source}`");
   599	            error.source_rewrite = Some(source);
   600	            error.source_rewrite_kind = Some(crate::diag::SourceRewriteKind::NamedUpdate);
   601	        }
   602	        // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.6 — the named form of a whole unnamed update rule, so the rewrite keeps every other clause.
   603	        if error.code == "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR" && rule.effect == Effect::Update && rule.bindings.is_empty() && error.rewrite.starts_with("name both images") {

   630	        error

   634	#[derive(Clone)]
   635	struct RuleBindings {
   636	    old: Option<String>,
   637	    next: Option<String>,
   638	    update: bool,
   639	    insert: bool,
   640	    hops: bool,
   641	    present: Vec<RuleTerm>,
   642	}
   643	
   644	// @ref LLP 3000.013#2.2 — presence facts retain a reference term's old/next image.
   645	// Facts hold on the logical edge where the next operand can affect truth.
   646	// Expiry accounting may evaluate other edges too: the shared runtime returns
   647	// no witness for an ordinary unique null key, without accessing tied rows.
   648	// Thus admission does not require physical short-circuiting. Facts still
   649	// cannot leak from one OR alternative into an unrelated alternative.
   650	fn present_terms(rule: &RuleExpr, truth: bool) -> Vec<RuleTerm> {
   651	    match rule {
   652	        RuleExpr::Ne(left, right) if truth => non_null_term(left, right),
   653	        RuleExpr::Eq(left, right) if !truth => non_null_term(left, right),
   654	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => present_terms(inner, !truth),
   655	        RuleExpr::And(parts) | RuleExpr::Or(parts) => {
   656	            let union = matches!(rule, RuleExpr::And(_)) == truth;
   657	            let mut facts = parts.iter().map(|part| present_terms(part, truth));
   658	            let mut result = facts.next().unwrap_or_default();
   659	            for facts in facts {
   660	                if union { for term in facts { if !result.contains(&term) { result.push(term); } } }
   661	                else { result.retain(|term| facts.contains(term)); }
   662	            }
   663	            result
   664	        }
   665	        _ => Vec::new(),
   666	    }
   667	}

   669	fn non_null_term(left: &RuleTerm, right: &RuleTerm) -> Vec<RuleTerm> {
   670	    match (left, right) {
   671	        (RuleTerm::Literal(Value::Null), term) | (term, RuleTerm::Literal(Value::Null)) => vec![term.clone()],
   672	        _ => Vec::new(),
   673	    }
   674	}

   676	fn rule_expr(catalog: &Catalog, info: &TableInfo, expr: &Expr, bindings: &RuleBindings) -> Fallible<RuleExpr> {

   682	            "public" => Ok(RuleExpr::Public { reason: format!("{} is public", info.decl.name) }),
   683	            "true" => Ok(RuleExpr::Allow),
   684	            "false" => Ok(RuleExpr::Deny),
   685	            other => Err(unknown(site, format!("`{other}` is not a rule; rules are allow, deny, public, exists, created, and comparisons over ., viewer and literals"), "read <- .ownerId = viewer")),

   815	fn rule_term(catalog: &Catalog, info: &TableInfo, expr: &Expr, bindings: &RuleBindings) -> Fallible<(RuleTerm, Ty)> {
   816	    let site = expr.site();
   817	    match expr {
   818	        Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" => Ok((RuleTerm::Viewer, Ty::Principal)),
   819	        Expr::Member { base, name, .. } => match base.as_ref() {
   820	            Expr::Read(read) if read.keys.len() == 1 && read.keys[0].column.as_deref().is_none_or(|c| c == "id")
   821	                && read.range.is_none() && read.filter.is_none() && read.matching.is_none()
   822	                && read.index.is_none() && read.seeks.is_empty() => {
   823	                let result = rule_reference(catalog, info, &read.keys[0].value, name, bindings, site)?;
   824	                if result.0.references().last().is_some_and(|(table, _)| table == read.table) { Ok(result) }
   825	                else { Err(type_error(site, "the lookup table differs from the reference type", "use the reference's declared table")) }
   826	            }
   827	            Expr::Focal { .. } => {
   828	                if bindings.update && bindings.old.is_some() {
   829	                    return Err(unknown(site, "an update (old, next) rule names its images; . is not bound", format!("next.{name}")));
   830	                }
   831	                let ty = column_ty(info, name).ok_or_else(|| unknown(site, format!("rule reads undeclared column {}.{name}", info.decl.name), name_rewrite(name, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None)))?;
   832	                Ok((RuleTerm::Field(name.clone()), ty))
   833	            }
   834	            Expr::Name { name: binder, .. } if bindings.old.as_deref() == Some(binder) => {
   835	                let ty = column_ty(info, name).ok_or_else(|| unknown(site, format!("rule reads undeclared column {}.{name}", info.decl.name), name_rewrite(name, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None)))?;
   836	                Ok((RuleTerm::OldField(name.clone()), ty))
   837	            }
   838	            Expr::Name { name: binder, .. } if bindings.next.as_deref() == Some(binder) => {
   839	                let ty = column_ty(info, name).ok_or_else(|| unknown(site, format!("rule reads undeclared column {}.{name}", info.decl.name), name_rewrite(name, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None)))?;
   840	                Ok((RuleTerm::NextField(name.clone()), ty))
   841	            }
   842	            Expr::Name { name: binder, .. } if bindings.update && bindings.old.is_none()
   843	                && matches!(binder.as_str(), "old" | "next") => Err(Diagnostic::new(site,
   844	                    "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR",
   845	                    format!("`{binder}.{name}` names a row image, but this update rule did not bind old and next"),
   846	                    "write this as a named transition").guide("rules")),
   847	            other => rule_reference(catalog, info, other, name, bindings, site),
   848	        },
   849	        Expr::Name { name, .. } if bindings.update && (bindings.old.as_deref() == Some(name) || bindings.next.as_deref() == Some(name)) => Err(unknown(site, format!("select a field of {name} explicitly"), format!("{name}.id"))),
   850	        Expr::Name { name, .. } => Err(unknown(site, format!("`{name}` is not a rule term; rules read the row as .{name}"), format!(".{name}"))),

   450	## 7. Formal and generated semantics
   451	
   452	The Lean table schema carries optional lower and upper lifetime fields. Its
   453	`live` projection filters every logical row lookup, scan, probe and write result
   454	at the case clock. Physical write-target lookup can still resolve an unopened,
   455	unexpired row, but an expired target is `NOT_FOUND`; an ordinary insert or
   456	upsert evaluates insert authority against the pre-retirement logical store,
   457	retires an expired same-id predecessor with its referential actions, then checks
   458	the new image's remaining unique keys against live occupants. `insert if absent`
   459	preflights all of those live unique-key collisions before same-id retirement; a
   460	collision is a no-op and preserves the expired predecessor and its children.
   461	The emitter includes both fields. The model's explicit physical sweep
   462	uses the same cascade/restrict/set-null closure as delete, retains a restricted
   463	root and continues to later due rows. It eagerly rematerializes the declared
   464	table snapshot after each retirement; this is extensionally the same sequential
   465	store update while avoiding an exponential functional-update expression tree.
   466	The Lean difftest generator preserves
   467	seeded expiry values and requested prelude/final sweeps, advances the formal
   468	store with each engine sweep, then compares the following program outcome.
   469	
   470	The difftest AST and generator produce null/past/future/equal-boundary openings,
   471	opening plus expiry, membership witnesses and caps. Its first formal fragment
   472	has no prelude or separately seeded clock: rows are seeded and evaluated under
   473	one operation clock with openings at null, clock-minus-one, clock, and
   474	clock-plus-one. That fragment proves the pure `live(now)` projection without
   475	claiming to model the durable pending ledger or its bounded publication loop.
   476	Native runtime, simulator and both device-store lifecycle suites cover
   477	lower/upper composition, publication, rescheduling, restart, hostile device
   478	clocks and server-floor rollback.

   481	
   482	The `time` and `recipes` cards carry one executable timed-disclosure recipe. It
   483	states separately:
   484	
   485	- use `not before .opensAt` to withhold a row until server time;
   486	- use a mutation `require now <|>= deadline else CODE` to authorize a timed
   487	  write;
   488	- a nullable opening means immediately readable, and `expire at` is the
   489	  independent upper boundary;
   490	- a device timer refreshes; it never unlocks secret data.

   321	else does.** The children's `delete` and `update` rules are not consulted,

   323	update's constraint check asks whether the writer can read the row; an
   324	action's write does not, so it draws nothing from the request's
   325	authorization allowance on a child's account).

   328	  project owner could never delete a project with a collaborator's task

   330	  unusable for the shared trees it exists for; and a refusal from a hidden
   331	  child's rule would tell the caller that a child it cannot read exists and
   332	  is not its own, which is more disclosure than `restrict`.
   333	- *The parent authorizes* is what SQL, Prisma and Rails do. It is sound here
   334	  because the schema says so explicitly, on the child's own column:

19-### Hops, operators and read through
20:Write rules and `after insert` keys allow three live hops: `.reaction.message.conversation`, including `exists members[.message.conversation, viewer]`. `messages[id = .message].conversation` is equivalent. Every target must be live and readable; absent, expired or hidden targets remain unknown under `not` and `= null`. Program lookups (`t[id] !`, `exists`) are reads too: a row the caller cannot read is NOT_FOUND there, before any later `require` or the delete/update rule runs, so give a moderator read access to what they moderate, or delete by id without a lookup and let the delete rule decide (`guide refusals` has the recipe). `check` notes N_UNREADABLE_PROBE on guards without proved read authority; use unique/cap/after insert constraints for global absence across hidden rows.
21-Each occurrence prepays one probe, including skipped branches. `check --cost`/`why` list them; prediction needs every read covered.
22-Insert uses the new image; an unnamed `update <- R` must hold for both the row before and the row after the write (pair `update <- .owner = viewer` with `immutable owner`); a named `update (old, next)` judges exactly what it names; delete uses its pre-delete image; final obligations resolve at transaction end. Read-through capture/lifetimes stay unchanged. Null guards narrow only the same term and image.

//! Final-exists misses need the same held-group proof as upsert absence.
use super::observation;
use super::super::common::*;
use serde_json::{Value as Json, json};
use snapback4_core::{Value, WriteState, wire};

const SOURCE: &str = r#"
table targets:
  owner: principal
  name: text <=10
  unique byName: name
  by byOwner: owner, name, id
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  sync
table sources:
  owner: principal
  name: text <=10
  unique byOwnerName: owner, name
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  update <- .owner = viewer
  after insert <- exists targets[name = .name]
  sync
mutation put():
  upsert sources[viewer, 'x'] {}
mutation add():
  insert sources {owner: viewer, name: 'x'}
query one():
  return sources[viewer, 'x']
table ballast:
  marker: bool
  online only
"#;

fn seeded(source: &str, owner: &str, name: Option<&str>) -> (snapback4_core::Engine, snapback4_device::device::Backend) {
    let (mut server, backend) = compile(source);
    // Give every world the same committed seed sequence, including absence.
    let mut rows = vec![("ballast".into(), wire::row_from_json(&server.schema().tables["ballast"], &json!({"id":"ballast", "marker":true})).unwrap())];
    if let Some(name) = name { rows.push(("targets".into(), wire::row_from_json(&server.schema().tables["targets"],
        &json!({"id":"target", "owner":owner, "name":name})).unwrap())); }
    server.seed(rows).unwrap();
    (server, backend)
}

fn unknown_worlds(op: &str, store: usize) {
    let mut worlds = Vec::new();
    for name in [None, Some("other"), Some("x")] {
        let (mut server, _) = seeded(SOURCE, "alice", name);
        let (result, observed) = observation::observe(&mut server, op, "bob", json!({}), "write", ("one", json!({})));
        if name == Some("x") {
            assert!(matches!(result.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{result:?}");
            assert_eq!(observed.devices[store]["settled"]["query"]["data"]["name"], "x");
        } else {
            assert!(matches!(result.state, WriteState::Failed { why, .. } if why.code == "E_CONSTRAINT"));
            assert_eq!(observed.devices[store]["settled"]["query"]["data"], Json::Null);
        }
        worlds.push(observed);
    }
    // The server's postcondition legitimately distinguishes a matching witness.
    // Its absent/nonmatching worlds still agree through receipts and settlement.
    worlds[0].assert_same(&worlds[1]);
    for world in &worlds[1..] {
        for stage in ["initial", "admission", "pending", "reopened"] {
            assert_eq!(worlds[0].devices[store][stage], world.devices[store][stage], "complete pre-settlement {stage}");
        }
    }
    for world in &worlds {
        let device = &world.devices[store];
        assert_eq!(device["admission"]["queued"]["predictable"], false, "store {store}: {}", device["admission"]);
        assert_eq!(device["admission"]["queued"]["predicted"], json!([]));
        assert_eq!(device["initial"]["rows"], device["pending"]["rows"], "no speculative row in any table");
        assert_eq!(device["pending"], device["reopened"], "complete pending state survives reopen");
        assert_eq!(device["pending"]["outbox"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(device["settled"]["outbox"], json!([]));
    }
}

#[test]
fn unpinned_upsert_sqlite() { unknown_worlds("put", 0); }
#[test]
fn unpinned_upsert_memory() { unknown_worlds("put", 1); }
#[test]
fn unpinned_insert_sqlite() { unknown_worlds("add", 0); }
#[test]
fn unpinned_insert_memory() { unknown_worlds("add", 1); }

fn held_worlds(op: &str, pinned: bool) {
    let source = if pinned { SOURCE.replace("unique byName: name", "unique byName: owner, name").replace("exists targets[name = .name]", "exists targets[viewer, .name]") }
        else { SOURCE.to_owned() };
    for present in [false, true] {
        // The unpinned case is the positive-hit control: finding the held row
        // needs no absence proof, even though this key cannot prove a miss.
        if !pinned && !present { continue; }
        let (mut server, _) = seeded(&source, "bob", present.then_some("x"));
        let (result, observed) = observation::observe(&mut server, op, "bob", json!({}), "write", ("one", json!({})));
        for device in &observed.devices {
            if present {
                assert!(matches!(&result.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{result:?}");
                assert_eq!(device["admission"]["queued"]["predictable"], true, "{}", device["admission"]);
                assert_eq!(device["admission"]["queued"]["predicted"], json!(["sources/fresh"]));
                let mut predicted = device["pending"]["query"]["data"].clone();
                assert_eq!(predicted.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("pending"), Some(json!(true)));
                assert_eq!(predicted, observed.body()["result"]);
                assert_eq!(predicted, device["settled"]["query"]["data"]);
            } else {
                let WriteState::Failed { why, .. } = &result.state else { panic!("{result:?}") };
                assert_eq!(why.code, "E_CONSTRAINT");
                assert_eq!(device["admission"]["refusal"], serde_json::to_value(why).unwrap(), "complete refusal matches the server");
                assert_eq!(device["pending"]["outbox"], json!([]));
                assert_eq!(device["pending"]["query"]["data"], Json::Null);
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn held_upsert_refusal_and_success_match_server() { held_worlds("put", true); }
#[test]
fn held_insert_refusal_and_success_match_server() { held_worlds("add", true); }
#[test]
fn unpinned_local_hits_still_predict() { held_worlds("put", false); held_worlds("add", false); }

#[test]
fn unknown_prediction_is_e_predict_on_both_stores() {
    fn run<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
        for op in ["put", "add"] {
            let (mut server, backend) = seeded(SOURCE, "alice", Some("x"));
            let mut device = host.open(op, Some(backend)).unwrap();
            for (i, page) in snapshot_pages(&mut server, "bob", 100).iter().enumerate() { device.apply(page, i == 0).unwrap(); }
            let error = device.predict(op, "bob", &json!({}), 1000, vec!["fresh".into()], 1).unwrap_err().refusal();
            println!("{} {op}: {}: {}", host.label(), error.code, error.message);
            assert_eq!(error.code, "E_PREDICT");
            assert_eq!(device.query("one", "bob", &json!({}), 1000).unwrap().data, Value::Null);
            host.close(op, device);
        }
    }
    run(&mut Sqlite::new("final-exists")); run(&mut Memory::new());
}

1. **Same-id replacement can violate live uniqueness.** [engine/write.rs:238](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:238) passes the retired, expired predecessor into constraint checks. The unchanged-key shortcut at [line 594](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:594) then skips secondary uniqueness. If expired `p` had key `K`, live `q` subsequently acquired `K`, and `p` is replaced with an unexpired image retaining `K`, the replacement commits two live occupants. Replacement must recheck live uniqueness after retirement.

2. **Commit-end cascades can invalidate already-passed final-exists obligations.** [engine/mod.rs:969](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/mod.rs:969) checks final-exists before retirement at [line 974](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/mod.rs:974). A mutation can insert an expired root, its live cascade child `c`, and a marker requiring `after insert <- exists children['c']`. The obligation passes; retirement then deletes `c`, and the marker commits without its required witness. Final obligations must cover the post-retirement state.

3. **Lean commit-end ordering changes commit/refusal outcomes.** [Quarry/Run.lean:74](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Run.lean:74) retains mutation-change order, consumed by [line 83](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Run.lean:83); runtime instead sorts by reverse table order and id at [engine/write.rs:512](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:512). Let one live child cascade from `aRoots` and restrict `zRoots`. Updating `aRoots` then `zRoots` to expire makes Lean retire `aRoots`, remove the blocker, and commit. Runtime visits `zRoots` first and rolls back with `E_REFERENCED`. The formal transition therefore disagrees with runtime on supported expiry/action semantics.
